title: report.json - a council run, structured
description: The machine-readable record of one finished council run: runs/<id>/report.json, built by reportJsonShape() in src/report-shape.js for every writer (a normal run, a resumed run, `council init`/`council demo`, --rematch, --replay). BOARD.md is the same record for people; nothing should parse BOARD.md. A run that stopped early (spend cap, pre-flight block, external pause, crash) writes no report.json at all - its absence means 'not finished'. A run the per-run spend cap stopped (since 0.7.7), and since 0.8.1 an advice call stopped by a person, its client or its wall clock (exit 18), writes runs/<id>/report-partial.json instead: this same schema, built by the same function from what the run had when it stopped, plus `partial: true`, `stoppedBy` and `stoppedAtStage`. In it a stage the run never reached has the value that means 'did not run' (null, [], false, or the field absent); `passed`, `outcome` and `signoff` describe the state at the stop, not a verdict; `finished_at` is when the run stopped. A resume removes it together with STOPPED-budget.json; a resumed run that finishes writes report.json. Versioning: `schemaVersion` is an integer that moves only on a breaking change (a field renamed, removed, or its meaning or type changed). Adding a field is not breaking and does not move it, so a reader MUST ignore fields it does not know; that is why additionalProperties is left open everywhere. Each top-level property carries an `x-stability` annotation: `stable` fields keep their name, type and meaning for the whole of schemaVersion 1; `experimental` fields may change shape in a minor release and are listed in the changelog when they do. Fields marked 'model-supplied' come from a model's own JSON reply and are passed through with little or no checking: read them defensively.

schemaVersion.description: Format version of this file. Integer; bumped only on a breaking change. Absent on report.json files written before 0.7.7: read those as version 1.

name.description: The npm package that wrote the file: the-high-council.

version.description: Its version, from its package.json ('unknown' if unreadable).

code_sha256.description: sha256 over the files the npm package ships, as present on disk: every .js, .mjs and .json file of the folders package.json "files" lists, minus its exclusions, by path and content, computed when the report was written. Two different stamps for one version mean the files on disk differed (a changed or an added file), not two harness versions. Added in 0.8.4. Absent where it cannot be computed (a packaged binary, an unreadable tree): never a partial hash.

sittings.description: One entry per sitting of the run that reached the chain, in order, from run.json: the first start and every resume. A start that leaves at the typed spending limit started nothing and has no entry. Added in 0.8.4; present on the report.json and report-partial.json of a run that began with it, and absent on a run that began before it and on the reports of --rematch, --replay and init.

version.description: The package version that ran it.

code_sha256.description: The code stamp of that sitting, as producer.code_sha256; absent where it cannot be computed.

producer.description: Which program, at which version, wrote this report. Added in 0.7.7; absent on earlier reports. 0.8.4 adds code_sha256 and sittings (additive).

started_at.description: When the run's first sitting began (ISO 8601, UTC). For --rematch, --replay and init: when that run began. Absent on reports written before 0.7.7, and on a resumed run whose first sitting predates 0.7.7 (its run.json never recorded the time).

finished_at.description: When this report was written (ISO 8601, UTC): the end of the run's last sitting. Added in 0.7.7; absent on earlier reports. Time spent paused at an external seat falls between the two timestamps.

runId.description: The run folder's name: an ISO-8601 timestamp with ':' and '.' replaced by '-' (e.g. 2026-09-25T15-08-53-698Z), plus a suffix for derived runs ('-init', '.rematch-<n>', '.replay-<date>').

chain.description: The chain config's `name` (chains/<name>.json). Names the recipe, not its contents: the chain file can change after the run.

task.description: Path to the task file, never absolute: relative to the directory the run was started in (forward slashes), or the file name alone when the file lies outside it. Written the same way by every writer since 0.7.7; earlier reports carry an absolute path after --resume, --rematch, --replay and init. Still names a file on the author's disk: consider dropping it before publishing a run.

task_sha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the task file's UTF-8 text as the report's last sitting read it. Its first 12 characters are run.json's `taskHash`, the frozen-scope check a resume makes. Lets a reader match a report to a task file without the path. On an advice run the task file is the brief, so this is the hash of the exact text every seat was sent (the text the person confirmed). Added in 0.7.7; absent on earlier reports.

fromRun.description: The earlier run folder whose criteria (and first draft) this run reused via --from-run; null when the run wrote its own. Never absolute since 0.7.7: relative to the directory the run was started in (forward slashes), or the run folder's name alone when it lies outside it. Earlier reports can carry an absolute path, notably after --resume.

criteria.description: Acceptance criteria, written before any draft or debate, in the order the panel was asked to check them. Model-supplied: the criteria stage checks that the list is non-empty and not meta, not that each item is a string.

questions.description: Clarifying questions the planner asked before writing criteria, each with its own default. null when the chain has no questions stage (and on a descending-mode run). Absent on descending-mode reports written before 0.7.7.

passed.description: True if the panel signed off on the final draft under the chain's sign-off rule (`first`: one critic; `unanimous`: every critic on the same draft). Read `outcome` before quoting this: a run can pass with part of its roster unheard. On a report that carries `advise` (an advice call, not a plan) this is not a sign-off: nobody reviewed a draft, it is true whenever the call ran, and verdict_stats and metrics skip such reports.

outcome.description: Verdict class, computed by src/outcome.js from the rest of this file. `degraded` wins: a seated lab produced nothing usable (it dropped out, see `dropouts[]`: in a tiered chain this may be a debating seat that never votes), a reviewer abstained, no reviewer was heard, or the round fell short of the quorum - so the run did not have the roster the chain intended. Otherwise `consensus` if passed, else `no_consensus`. On a report that carries `advise` this is not a sign-off either: it says whether the advisors' answers agreed (see `advise`), and verdict_stats and metrics skip such reports. On a layered run with an `ending` (0.8.4) `consensus` also needs that ending to be agreed: a top-layer sign-off that does not end agreed (the handler said not yet, the delivered text is not the text the top layer signed, or a final read objected) reads `no_consensus` although `passed` is true, and an escalated sign-off the handler agreed reads `no_consensus` too (the agreement lives in `ending` and the exit code). With no `ending` the rule is unchanged.

lastCritique.description: The last review round's verdict. Unanimous chains: the union of every critic's failures, each tagged with `lab`. First-to-pass chains: the one critic's own parsed reply. null only if no review round ran.

signoff.description: One entry per critic seat ASKED in the final unanimous round (all of them on a flat panel). On a layered run (see `layers`) a seat whose layer was not asked in that round has no entry here: read `layers` for the layers that were never asked, and never infer a pass from this array alone. null on chains whose sign-off is `first` (see panelVerdicts for those).

proposals.description: Every proposal kept for the debate, one node per proposal. Empty when the chain has no proposal stage. A lab that produced none is not here: see dropouts.

dropouts.description: Seats that were on the roster but produced nothing usable (unreadable proposals after a retry, a provider failure in review). Count labs from here plus proposals, never from proposals alone.

excerpts.description: Additive. Present in the finished report.json only, and only when the run recorded a line in excerpts.jsonl (a stopped or partial run's report-partial.json carries no excerpts entry): how many lines the file holds (an excerpt of project text the seats were shown, or a request that was declined, left unanswered, withheld or not cut) and the sha256 of the file as it is. The format of a line is schemas/excerpts-v1.json.

roster_answers.description: Present only when the run had a session-seat stage (provider external). Who answered those stages, AS DECLARED by the MCP client and the session, never verified, and the review panel's company count as recorded beside the count the chain was designed for. A seat answered by a different model is not a dropout and does not change outcome. Added 0.8.3.

design_companies.description: Companies on the review panel by what the chain asks for.

recorded_companies.description: Companies on the review panel by what was recorded: model-API seats by their model, session seats by the model their answer declared.

panel_session_seats.description: Present only when a stage of the review panel was answered through a session seat: how many stages that was. Nothing checks that those stages were answered by separate sessions.

unverified_seats.description: Session seats on the panel whose answer declared no model, or one this version has no company for.

company.description: The company of the declared model, or null when none was declared or this version has no row for it.

panel.description: True for a stage of the review panel (a judge): only these count in the company tally. Writer stages (build, revise, handoff) are listed but counted nowhere.

status.description: no-model-asked: the seat asks for no particular model (claude-code-session); never 'different' and never 'not-declared'.

debate.description: The anonymised argument over the proposals: posts (who said what about which proposal) and replies (what each author then did). null when the chain has no debate stage.

scoreboard.description: What the final plan did with each proposal, read from the plan's own 'Scope ledger' lines, per proposal and per lab. null when there were no proposals (and on a descending-mode run). Absent on descending-mode reports written before 0.7.7.

totals.description: Token and cost totals over every stage in `stages`, plus any superseded stages paid for earlier.

superseded.description: Optional. Present only when stages were set aside and paid for again: the superseded records `totals.supersededUsd` absorbed when this report was written, one { label, usd, reservationId } each (label is the file under superseded/; reservationId is null for a record written before 0.8.3), so the share of the total stays attributable if a file is later lost. Added in 0.8.3.

kind.description: Present on a charge record: waste (a discarded attempt) or billed (a call that was sent and may have been billed).

unreplayed.description: Optional. Present only when paid stage files that no stages[] row accounts for were found: the files `totals.unreplayedUsd` absorbed when this report was written, one { label, usd, reservationId } each (reservationId is null for a file written before 0.8.3). Added in 0.8.4.

maxUsd.description: The per-run spend ceiling in USD this run was held to (--max-usd, MAX_USD_PER_RUN, or the default); null when the ceiling was disabled (--max-usd none), when the run ran under one spending cap per provider (see caps), or, for init/rematch/replay, not recorded.

caps.description: Present only when the run ran under one spending cap per provider (COUNCIL_SPEND_CAPS): for each cap, the limit typed for it (maxUsd) and what the run spent through it (spentUsd).

stages.description: One record per model call, in the order they were recorded (concurrent calls may interleave). The reply text itself is in <label>.md in the run folder, not here.

alternatives.description: Present only on chains with alternatives.enabled: one whole architecture per lab, written blind before the skeleton, and the same post/reply board the proposals get.

deep_dive.description: Present only on chains with deep_dive.enabled (tiered councils): the one deep-dive seat's calls, its own dollar cap, what it spent, why it stopped (null, own_cap or max_calls) and its findings, each with a quote_status. The findings are not votes; under "judging": "all-roles" the same lab may also judge on the panel.

spending_finish.description: 0.8.4: present only on a run the person ended at its spending limit with finish-now, in every phase (a stop after the review rounds makes no `stop`, so this is the record of the person's choice). phase: loop | after; label: the stage the limit stopped; cap_name: the cap that stopped it, when per-provider caps were armed. Accepting such a plan is the person's.

relayed.description: 0.8.4: present (true) when the person's finish-now was relayed by the handling session with the person's words (the ledger line says so, with the gate that holds the words).

kept_limits.description: 0.8.4: present only on a run the person ended at its spending limit with finish-now. Each spending limit the run stopped at, kept in force in that command (read from the record of what the person typed), with what the run had counted against it in dollars. cap_name is null for the run's one limit.

stages_not_run.description: 0.8.4: present only on a run the person ended with finish-now at its spending limit, or at a found-secret pause. Every call that was not made because the person ended the run (at the spending limit: one that would bill, or a judge's read that is not on disk; at a pause: a judge's read that is not on disk), by its stage label; the plan and the verdict are what the run had reached without them. A seat the final read did not ask has its own row in final_read.seats[] (not_run).

reason.description: spending_limit: the person ended the run at the spending limit. finished_at_once: the person ended the run at once at a pause, and a judge's read that is not on disk was not made (0.8.4).

anyOf.description: Not raised (raised false), or (0.8.4) not run: the person finished the run at once and the challenge would have been asked of a judge of the panel (no challenger seat is set), so it was not run (ran false, reason finished_at_once). One member, so the 0.8.0 shape of this property (three alternatives) is unchanged.

decision.description: Model-supplied: the decision the challenger re-opened.

evidence_needed.description: Model-supplied: what evidence would settle it.

reopened_rounds.description: Always 1 today: one challenge re-opens one decision for one round.

challenge.description: Post-sign-off challenge stage (challenge.enabled). null when the chain does not enable it.

engaged.description: False when the reviser left the draft byte-for-byte unchanged (a rubber stamp).

allocator.description: Extra rounds aimed at the most contested criterion (allocator.enabled). null when off.

round.description: A review round number, or one of the strings 'build' (the builder's own DECLINED lines, since 0.8.1), 'dispute', 'challenge', 'allocator-<n>' for text written outside the numbered rounds. Mixed type: see the report's fix list.

reason.description: Model-supplied: why the reviser declined this objection.

objection_id.description: The id of the objection this DECLINED line answered, when the reviser named one (a chain with answer_back.enabled whose prompt asks for it). Absent when it named none. Added in 0.8.2.

disputes.description: Objections the builder or the reviser declined and kept out of the deliverable (their DECLINED lines). Not the same thing as `dispute`.

orphanSections.description: Sections left with no surviving owner after a withdrawal chain cycled or dead-ended. [] on a descending-mode run; absent on descending-mode reports written before 0.7.7.

withdrawalCycles.description: How many withdrawal chains cycled (e.g. two labs withdrawing in each other's favour). 0 on a descending-mode run; absent on descending-mode reports written before 0.7.7.

sorting.description: Additive (0.8.4): a top-layer seat's sorting of the objections open at its verdict: each row an objection id sorted must_do or may_leave for the build, with the seat's reason; a must_do with no criterion and no decision is flagged ungrounded. Present only when the chain keeps the answer_back ledger and demands ratings, and the reply carried rows.

rating.description: 0.8.4, additive: the seat's rating of an unanchored failure it sorted must-do (present only on such a row); it is the rating of the late finding made from it.

route.description: Additive (0.8.4): the repair route the seat named for a must-do: writer, or proposers (the decision would go back to the proposers). A closing read only recommends it; nothing is sent back at a read. On a combined row: proposers when any seat's must-do named it, else writer.

route_asked.description: Additive (0.8.4): proposers, when a seat asked for the proposers on a chain that has no proposer seat; the route is then recorded as writer and nothing is asked again.

route_unread.description: Additive (0.8.4): what the seat wrote as the route when it was neither writer nor proposers; it is not read as a route.

reasons_shown_in.description: Additive (0.8.4): the round in which the objection's raiser was first shown this seat's reason, as escalations[].outcome[].reasons_shown_in says for a ruling. Present only when the raiser's review carried it.

sorting_new.description: Additive (0.8.4): new defects this top-layer seat named only in its sorting at its verdict: each a must_do entry with a reason and an id outside the list, or with no id and the passage it is about, kept whole (reason, quote, criterion or decision). They are recorded here, and while the seat is asked again it can raise them as objections. At the seat's last verdict (its latest verdict given when asked: a later carried row is not a new verdict, and a later unheard or unreadable one is not a withdrawal) each is also recorded as a late finding, one per text (found is last_verdict).

rating.description: Additive (0.8.4): the seat's rating of this defect, 1 to 10, when it gave a valid one.

ungrounded_why.description: Additive (0.8.4): why this defect is ungrounded as a late finding, read against the plan the seat read when it gave the verdict: no_criterion, no_quote or quote_not_in_plan; null when it is grounded. (ungrounded, beside it, is the sorting's own rule: the entry names no criterion and no decision.)

sorting_ignored.description: Additive (0.8.4): how many rows of that sorting were ignored: an unknown sort, an id already given, a may-leave of an id that was not in the list the seat was shown, a must-do of one with no reason, an entry with no id that is not a must-do with a reason and the passage it is about, or a sorting that was not a list. Present only when above zero.

cut.description: 0.8.4, additive: true on the row of a seat that had answered, in the layer or panel being asked, when the person's finish ended the run (at a pause for a credential-shaped string, or at the spending limit); on a layered chain the run's stop is of kind secret_pause or budget_stop. The reply is the seat's own and stays on the record; it counts for no sign-off and no read. Its objections count as open, except one the seat withdrew in a completed round of the exchange the finish cut: signed_text.open_objections counts the open ones, and where the report carries a dispute record, dispute.open_objections lists them. Of those, one the seat already held open before the finish keeps the row it had; any other is marked cut_off. The withdrawn one is closed: it is not counted or listed, and its withdrawal is recorded in answer_back_replies (where the chain keeps the answer-back ledger) and, unless the objection was first named in a post of that exchange, in the severity record (where it keeps ratings).

exchange_cleared.description: 0.8.4, additive: the verdict is signed_off because every objection of this judge was withdrawn in its layer's exchange; on a verdict carried from an earlier pass, it was cleared in the pass it came from.

swept_only.description: 0.8.4, additive, only on a layered chain with "signoff": "unanimous" whose judges rate their objections: the verdict is signed_off although it lists objections, every one rated below the line that holds a sign-off (swept); told apart from a clean sign-off.

exchange_changed.description: 0.8.4, additive: set on a verdict carried from an earlier pass that THIS pass's exchange changed (a new objection named in a post).

defect_named.description: 0.8.4, additive: the verdict is a sign-off that named a defect of its own in an exchange post of this pass. The blind sign-off is kept; the defect is the seat's own open objection (signoff[].holds_layer says whether it holds the layer).

sustained.description: Stall escalation: the passed-up objection ids this seat sustained in its ruling; it then holds them as its own, so its verdict reads objected whatever its blind review said.

lane.description: 0.8.2 (item 7): the review lane of this seat, present only when the seat has one (the optional plan-lanes-4 chain).

pass_reason.description: 0.8.4, additive: on a row with verdict `passed` of a chain that reviews one critic per round (no `signoff: unanimous`) whose `freedoms.pass` is set: the reason the critic gave for declining to judge the draft (capped); the plan was not revised after it; the next round's critic, if there was one, read it unchanged.

envelope.description: Present only on an unheard row of a run that used the verdict envelope (see `verdict_envelope`), and only when the reply was a complete JSON object that carried no review_id and draft_id for this call (`missing`) or ids that were not this call's (`wrong_id`). A reply that was cut off, ended by an error, ran out of reasoning or was not a JSON object at all keeps its `reason_code` and has no `envelope`: its absence never means the ids were fine. `reason_code` keeps its own value.

no_answer.description: Present only on an unheard seat whose reply was cut off at its cap after spending its tokens on thinking and carried no text: "no answer: thinking used the whole cap". The seat is unheard (an unreadable non-pass), never a pass. Added in 0.8.1.

table_gap.description: Present only on an unheard seat refused for an incomplete sign-off table (reason_code INCOMPLETE_TABLE, chains with signoff_table.required): what the table lacked. Added in 0.8.2.

reasked.description: True if a re-ask call was made for this seat this round. False otherwise, even when its first reply was not counted.

carried.description: Present and true when the seat was not asked this round: the draft was byte-identical to the last round's, where this seat was heard and clean, and only the unheard seat(s) were asked again (0.7.9). Absent otherwise.

layer.description: 0.8.3: the layer the seat sits in. Present only on a layered chain. A seat whose layer was not asked in a round has NO row here for that round; `layers` records it as not_asked.

from_round.description: 0.8.3: on a carried verdict of a layered chain, the round in which the verdict was given (no new call, no new charge).

panelVerdicts.description: Every critic's verdict in every review round, both sign-off modes. The per-round history that signoff[] (final round only) does not keep.

regressions.description: Criteria that had been met and then failed again in a later round, with the labs that failed them.

final_read.description: Additive, present on every run of a unanimous layered chain that reaches its end: the final read by the top layer at the end of a run, agreed or not. ran false carries a reason (every_top_seat_read_this_plan: every top-layer seat had already read exactly this plan; finished_at_once, 0.8.4: the person finished the run at a stop with finish-now, so no seat was asked; at the stop for a plan no top-layer seat could read, a run that had not agreed before the read has ran true, no seat read, and ends not agreed at once, while a run that had agreed keeps that verdict and the read is recorded as owed and not made); otherwise each top-layer seat that had not read the final plan was asked once (re-asked once on an unreadable reply); where the chain keeps the answer_back ledger and demands ratings, a run that ended without agreement also asks a seat that had read this plan but was not shown an objection or late finding opened or amended since its last sorting (its last_read_sha equals final_sha). A record of what each seat said. It never changes passed, signoff[] or panelVerdicts. In a run that had ended agreed it does change the reported ending: an objection in the final read that holds the sign-off (an objection rated 4 or above, or without a rating) turns it into no consensus; otherwise a top-layer seat that did not read the final plan turns it into degraded (a verdict never reached); with neither, the ending stays agreed. The outcome word, the exit code, the verdict line and the BOARD banner follow. final_sha is the 12-hex id of the plan body that was read (the same hash as the verdict envelopes' draft_id).

handler_sort_not_run.description: 0.8.4: the final read split the top layer (one seat objected, another signed this text) and the person ended the run at once, so the handling session was not asked to sort the objection: it stays unsorted.

relayed.description: 0.8.4: present (true) with reason finished_at_once when the person's finish-now was relayed by the handling session.

coverage_only.description: Additive (0.8.4): present (true) with reason finished_at_once only when every top-layer seat had already read exactly this plan and one more read was owed, because an objection or late finding was opened or amended since a seat's last sorting; that read was not made.

run_end.description: How the run had ended BEFORE the final read: agreed (every layer signed off, or layer 3 signed off and the handler said good to build) or not_agreed (the run ended without agreement). An escalated or ladder sign-off that the handler agreed reads agreed here. This value does not move. In a run that had ended agreed, the final read can change the reported ending: an objection that holds the sign-off (an objection rated 4 or above, or without a rating) turns it into no consensus; otherwise a top-layer seat that did not read the final plan turns it into degraded; with neither, the ending stays agreed. The outcome word, the exit code and the BOARD banner follow; passed and signoff[] are never changed.

decided_by.description: 0.8.4, additive: present when a layer-3 seat objected to the final plan and the run has no handling session: nobody decided the objection; it stays open and counts as must-do for the build.

basis.description: Additive (0.8.4): final_read_objection, present only when the run had ended without agreement (run_end not_agreed), the final read ran, and a top-layer seat that was asked at that read answered it with an objection that blocks a sign-off: a failure rated 4 or above, a failure with no readable rating, or an objection that names no failure. The failures it named are in seats[].failures[], each with its rating when it gave a readable one. A seat whose earlier read was reused (it is in reused[], not in seats[]) never sets it. Absent otherwise: on an agreed run, when the read did not run, and when every asked seat signed off, did not read, or objected only with failures that are all rated below 4. A run that has an ending record also lists its own reasons in ending.basis[].

not_run.description: 0.8.4: this seat was not asked because the person ended the run (spending_limit: at the spending limit; finished_at_once: at once at a pause) and its read of this plan is not on disk; it counts as a seat that did not read.

reask_not_run.description: 0.8.4: this seat was asked (its reply is on disk) and gave no usable reply, and it was not asked again because the person ended the run (at the spending limit, or at once at a pause); it counts as a seat that did not read.

quote.description: Additive (0.8.4): the passage of the final plan this objection quotes, word for word.

not_debated.description: Additive (0.8.4): true. An objection of the final read is never debated: no exchange follows the read.

open.description: 0.8.4, additive: present on an objection of the final read that holds the sign-off (rated 4 or above, or not rated): it stays open on the record under the seat's name with its own rating, never deleted or re-rated, and counts as must-do for the build. An objection rated below 4 carries no mark: it is recorded and ends nothing.

concern.description: Additive (0.8.4): a note this top-layer seat attached to its final read for the build to watch, in its own words (at most 8000 characters, the cap of every field a judge writes). It does not claim that a criterion fails: it is not an objection and not a late finding, carries no rating, holds nothing back, is never debated or declined. Present only when the seat wrote one.

label.description: The call label of the part as the call carried it in the run log and the spend record (a part that was split ends -h1 or -h2; the label of a re-ask, which ends -reask1, is not used).

why.description: The cause, in the sentence form of this entry's own `why`: no reply, an unreadable reply, a reply with no sorting list, or the provider refusing the prompt for its size even with one item in it.

parts_unread.description: Additive (0.8.4): one entry for each part of a long list that this seat could not be read on, in the order the parts were asked. Present only when a part was not read. Its objections have no word from this seat: the combined sorting reads a seat that gave no word as must-do. Its late findings have no word from this seat either: a late finding is sorted only by a seat that read it.

sorting_ignored.description: Additive (0.8.4): how many rows of this seat's sorting were ignored: an unknown sort, an id already given, a may-leave of an id that was not in the list the seat was shown, a must-do of one with no reason, an entry with no id that is not a must-do with a reason and the passage it is about, or a sorting that was not a list. A must-do with a reason and an id outside the list, or no id and the passage, is a new defect and is in sorting_new, not here. Present only when above zero.

sorting_new.description: Additive (0.8.4): new defects this top-layer seat found at its read that no listed item names: each a must_do entry with an id outside the list, or with no id and the passage it is about, kept whole (reason, quote, criterion or decision). Each is also recorded as a late finding, one per text. Present only when the sorting was on and the reply carried one.

rating.description: Additive (0.8.4 S16): the seat's rating of this defect, 1 to 10, when it gave a valid one at the final read.
0.8.4, additive: the seat's rating of an unanchored failure it sorted must-do (present only on such a row); it is the rating of the late finding made from it.

route.description: Additive (0.8.4): the repair route the seat named for a must-do: writer, or proposers (the decision would go back to the proposers). A closing read only recommends it; nothing is sent back at a read. On a combined row: proposers when any seat's must-do named it, else writer.

route_asked.description: Additive (0.8.4): proposers, when a seat asked for the proposers on a chain that has no proposer seat; the route is then recorded as writer and nothing is asked again.

route_unread.description: Additive (0.8.4): what the seat wrote as the route when it was neither writer nor proposers; it is not read as a route.

sorting.description: Additive (0.8.4): this top-layer seat's sorting of the open objections at its read: each row an objection id sorted must_do or may_leave for the build, with the seat's reason; a must_do with no criterion and no decision is flagged ungrounded. Present only when the chain keeps the answer_back ledger and demands ratings, and the reply carried rows.

rating.description: 0.8.4, additive: the seat's rating of an unanchored failure it sorted must-do (present only on such a row); it is the rating of the late finding made from it.

route.description: Additive (0.8.4): the repair route the seat named for a must-do: writer, or proposers (the decision would go back to the proposers). A closing read only recommends it; nothing is sent back at a read. On a combined row: proposers when any seat's must-do named it, else writer.

route_asked.description: Additive (0.8.4): proposers, when a seat asked for the proposers on a chain that has no proposer seat; the route is then recorded as writer and nothing is asked again.

route_unread.description: Additive (0.8.4): what the seat wrote as the route when it was neither writer nor proposers; it is not read as a route.

sorting.description: Additive (0.8.4): the top-layer seats' sortings combined, one row per objection id: may_leave only when EVERY top-layer seat's closing word on it (its own sorting at the final read, or for a seat that did not need to read, its sorting at its last verdict) is may_leave, otherwise must_do (an objection a seat gave no word on counts as must-do; the build may get more than it needs); ungrounded when no seat's must_do names a criterion or a decision; seats and reasons list who sorted it and why, each seat's own word unchanged.

by.description: 0.8.4, additive: present on a combined row that the handling session sorted at the wait for an objection of the final read: its sort replaces the raiser's own must-do, the row's reasons hold both (the raiser's own and the handler's), and every other top-layer seat's sign-off is in final_read.seats or final_read.reused. The objection stays open under the seat's name with its own rating.

route.description: Additive (0.8.4): the repair route the seat named for a must-do: writer, or proposers (the decision would go back to the proposers). A closing read only recommends it; nothing is sent back at a read. On a combined row: proposers when any seat's must-do named it, else writer.

route_asked.description: Additive (0.8.4): proposers, when a seat asked for the proposers on a chain that has no proposer seat; the route is then recorded as writer and nothing is asked again.

route_unread.description: Additive (0.8.4): what the seat wrote as the route when it was neither writer nor proposers; it is not read as a route.

unanchored.description: true when the objection quotes no passage of the plan; it stays an objection.

reused.description: Additive (0.8.4): the top-layer seats that were not asked because they had already read exactly this plan, each with the verdict of its last read and the round it was given in. Present only when the sorting is on and a seat was not asked.

sorting.description: Additive (0.8.4): the sorting that seat gave with its last verdict, when that verdict carried one.

reason.description: escalated_signoff (0.8.4, stall escalation; a closed enum widened: a reader that validates `reason` strictly must accept it): the top layer signed off with lower layers passed over (see escalated_signoff); the dispute stage runs over the passed-up objections no ruling closed, except after the handler's good_to_build, when it does not run (`ran` false with this reason); a pass the handler routed to layer 3 that layer 3 signed ends with this reason too, and the dispute stage then runs over the open objections of the layers that were not asked; a sign-off under the ladder carries this reason too, though no stall led to it and nothing was passed up in that pass. stalled (narrowed in 0.8.4): a stall that ENDED the loop on an unlayered chain; on a layered chain a stall that cannot be passed up (the top layer holds it; no pass is left; the chain keeps no answer-back list or does not ask its judges to rate; or the next pass is a ladder pass, which does not pass a plan up) stops the run for the person's choice instead (see `stop`, kind stall_stop); a stall that was passed up is in escalations instead. early_finish (0.8.3, a closed enum widened: a reader that validates `reason` strictly must accept it): the run finished early at the session's proposal with the overseer layer's yes (see `stop`); no round cap was reached. layer_not_signed_off (0.8.3): a layered run stopped because a layer gave no usable verdict or the top layer did not sign off explicitly (see layerStop). finish_chosen (0.8.3): the person chose to finish after the run stopped at an overseer or layer limit, or at a stall (see `stop`). rule_no_handler (0.8.4, a closed enum widened: a reader that validates `reason` strictly must accept it): the run has no handling session, so nobody could choose at its overseer-round limit or at a silent seat of layer 1 or 2, and it ended at that stop, not agreed, after the final read (see `stop`, chosen "rule"). Never set on a chain whose seats are all mock.

not_asked_in_final_round.description: 0.8.3, layered chains: the lab raised this in last_raised_round and its layer was not asked in the final round, so it may already be fixed in the final draft.

cut_off.description: 0.8.4, additive: the lab raised this in last_raised_round, in a judge reply that the person's finish cut off or in a completed round of the exchange the finish cut (the lab's row in panelVerdicts is marked cut). The objection is open and listed for the person to answer; no judge and no writer was asked about it after the finish.

dissent.description: Additive (0.8.4). true on an objection that is also a dissent (see `dissents`).

escalated_standing.description: Stall escalation: this objection stood unchanged up to last_raised_round, was passed up a layer, and no ruling closed it (see escalations).

closed_by.description: Additive (0.8.4): final_read, when the top layer's closing read closed this objection after the dispute stage ran: every top-layer seat sorted it may-leave, and it is rated below 4 and was never rated 7 or above. The entry stays in this list as the dispute stage recorded it, except that it no longer carries `dissent` (a closed objection is not a dissent); the seats' sorting and reasons are in final_read.sorting or final_read.reused[].sorting. A reader that counts what is open at the run's end leaves a marked entry out.

review.description: Present when the chain sets dispute.review: per-objection checks of how the draft handled it.

rewrite_not_run.description: 0.8.4: the person ended the run at the spending limit, and the dispute stage's rewrite of the plan would bill, so it was not made; the open objections are recorded all the same.

review_not_run.description: 0.8.4: the chain sets dispute.review and the person finished the run at once, so the judges that raised the objections were not asked again.

dispute.description: Present only on chains with dispute.enabled: whether the dispute stage ran, why, and the objections left open (recorded at the top of the deliverable).

title.description: Model-supplied proposal title, or null if the id is unknown.

posts.description: The debate posts on this proposal, without `on` (it is the group's).

disagreement_groups.description: Present only when the run debated: the debate's posts grouped by the proposal they argue about. Derived from debate and proposals; adds no new facts.

result.description: The tool's own result: ok, exitCode, stdout, stderr and so on.

ground_truth.description: Present only on chains with verify.enabled: allowlisted tool results shown verbatim to later stages.

lints.description: Present only on chains with lints.enabled: deterministic plan lints. Informational, never a failure.

claims.description: Present only on chains with claims.enabled: objections restated with typed evidence. Claims whose evidence failed the offline check are dropped (and listed in WARNINGS.md).

warnings.description: 0.8.2, additive: a check that did not refuse the run but is worth knowing (max_usd_per_run: the expected cost fits the limit, the dry run's maximum is over it). Absent when there was none.

policy.description: Present only when a policy.json was in force: the checks it configured. Absent means no policy.

seat_personas.description: Additive, present only when the chain's seat_personas switch is on: which persona each seat carried (judges first, then proposers, whose layer is null) and every place a persona name appears in judge-written text (counted, never redacted).

kind.description: Whether the seat is a judge (seats.critics) or a proposer (seats.proposers). Added 0.8.4, additive.

personas_source.description: Additive, present only when a debate prompt was built from the persona set. Where that set came from: default (no file configured), file (a configured file was read and parsed to an object), fallback (a file was configured but could not be read or parsed, so the shipped set was used without a message); null when the stage rows that carried a set name different sets, because then each row's own `persona_set_sha256` is the record and the run claims none.

personas_sha256.description: Additive, present with personas_source: the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (keys sorted, no whitespace) of the persona set the debate prompts were built from; it never holds the operator's file path or the voice text. null when the stage rows that carried a set name different sets (a persona file edited during the run, or between a pause and its answer's sitting): each row's `persona_set_sha256` is then the record.

personas_used.description: Additive, present with personas_source: the persona keys the run's debating seats name, in seat order, once each.

severity.description: Additive, present on every layered chain with "signoff": "unanimous": the severity record of the run (its lines carry no rating until the judges are asked to rate their objections). An objection rated 4 or above holds a sign-off (4 to 6.9 is the settle band, 7 to 10 the fix band); one rated below 4 does not hold it (swept). Whatever its band, the hold is released only by the raiser's own argued withdrawal, which closes the objection (in the layer exchange, or in the answer-back with a passage copied from the revised draft, which is how a fix is recorded), or by a re-tag below 4 from the top layer or the handler session, which takes the hold off the objection without closing it; nothing else releases one. `computed` is false when the run stopped before the end of its last pass was reached: `open_at_end` then lists the objections open as of the last pass that was computed and `as_of_pass` names that pass, or `open_at_end` is null with `not_computed` saying why; it is never an empty list that reads as clean. `overrides` lists every later claim of another value for an objection whose first valid tag stands (a downgrade is a judge lowering its own objection and being refused). `withdrawn` lists each withdrawal with the ORIGINAL tag. An objection that was once rated 7 or above and that a re-tag has put below 4 no longer holds a sign-off, but it is not closed: it stays listed in `open_at_end`, with its rating below 4 and its re-tags in `retags`, until it is fixed or its raiser withdraws it, and `invariant` is not set for such a row. `retags` lists the re-tags that applied, each with who made it (`by`: layer3, with the seat's row, or handler, also listed in owner_retags) and the value that applied; `retags_refused` lists the ones refused, with why.

asked.description: True when the judges were asked to rate their objections; false when they were not. When it is false no one was asked, so every objection reads unrated and its band is `unreadable`: that is the absence of an asked rating, not a broken reply. When it is true, `unreadable` means a rating that could not be read.

unheard_at_end.description: The seats that gave no usable reply in the last pass: their last known objections are in the list, anything new they would have said is not.

invariant.description: Set when a run that PASSED still lists an objection that holds a sign-off: a defect of the harness, recorded loudly.

cleared_by.description: 0.8.4: the route by which it cleared. withdrawal: the raiser took it back (in the exchange, or in its answer-back with a quote from another reviewer). fix: the raiser's answer-back withdrew it with a quote that is found in the REVISED draft, whichever fix the writer took.

raiser_seat.description: Additive (0.8.4, same-layer seats): the seat key of the objection's raiser when it differs from the lab; `seat` stays the layer-3 seat that re-tagged.

cleared_by.description: 0.8.4: set on the re-tag that put the objection below 4 and left it there (the route by which it cleared).

gate.description: A handler re-tag: the approval gate it was relayed through (see owner_retags).

picked_by.description: Additive (0.8.4): present on every layer-3 row of an objection that two or more top-layer seats re-rated to different values in one pass when the handling session picked one of their ratings; `applied_to` is the picked value.

pick_reason.description: Additive (0.8.4): the handling session's reasons for that pick.

makers.description: 0.8.4: the maker (the model's company) of each critic seat, by seat key; record only, never weighed. A seat with no maker (a mock seat, a session seat that names no model) is not listed, and the key is absent when no seat has one. An objection's rating, every change of it (overrides, retags) and the route by which it cleared (withdrawn[].cleared_by, retags[].cleared_by; an objection in open_at_end has not cleared) are read beside it.

by.description: Present on a refused handler re-tag (it has no seat).

gate.description: Judged from the findings, never from the seat's own verdict. not_judged is never a pass.

security_review.description: Present only on chains with security_review.enabled: the final read-only security gate. Same object as security-review.json in the run folder.

on.description: Proposal id the canary objection was posted on.

capitulated.description: True if the author amended or withdrew in answer to an evidence-free objection.

no_quote_mark.description: Only in a chain with debate_hygiene.noQuoteMarks: true when the canary was shown to the author through the "[no quote]" mark like every other post that quotes nothing, false when the reply prompt in use did not render marks. Capitulation rates are not comparable across the two without saying so. Added in 0.8.2.

canary.description: Present only when a canary objection was sampled into the debate (canary.enabled). The canary post and reply are also in debate.posts/replies, each with canary: true and by: 'canary'.

quoteFindings.description: Present when the task fenced source text: one human-readable line per objection whose quote could not be found in that source, or that quoted nothing. Nothing is dropped because of these.

patchFallbacks.description: Present on chains with revise.mode 'patch': rounds where the reviser's patch could not be applied and a whole-draft revision was used instead.

status.description: 0.8.2: not_judged when the seat could not be reached or its reply could not be read; raised is then false but that is NOT 'no contradictions' - nobody did the check. Absent on a report written before 0.8.2 (read it as judged).

reason_code.description: 0.8.2: why the cold read is not_judged.

coldRead.description: Present only on chains with coldRead.enabled: a fresh seat that saw only the final draft (since 0.8.2, the text that is delivered, after any final edit), listing contradictions between its sections. Its findings, or the fact that it was not judged, are also written into the deliverable and WARNINGS.md.

layer.description: 0.8.3: on a layered chain, the layer in which nobody was heard.

noHeardReviewer.description: Present only when a review round heard no reviewer at all and the loop stopped there. Makes outcome 'degraded'.

overseer_round.description: 0.8.3, present only on a chain with overseer rounds (maxOverseerRounds): the overseer round this pass belongs to. A round ends only when the top layer gives a verdict; `round` stays the pass number and the stage labels never change.

state.description: signed_off: every seat of the layer was heard and clear (a seat whose objections are all rated below 4 counts as clear). objected: a seat raised an objection that holds the sign-off (an objection rated 4 or above, or without a rating). unheard: nobody objected but a seat was not heard. abstained: asked, but no usable verdict (only stated passes, or in the top layer a seat that did not sign off explicitly). not_asked: a layer below did not sign off, so this one was not started; or the ladder started the pass above this layer; or the ladder passed this layer over because it had used its visits; or the pass was asked to start at layer 3 by a request. unfinished: asked and interrupted (a stop, a cap, a wall clock) before it finished. escalated (0.8.4, stall escalation; a closed enum widened: a reader that validates `state` strictly must accept it): not asked because objections that stood unchanged were passed up from this layer or one below it; the layers below the floor wait until the top layer gives a verdict (see escalations).

sustained.description: Stall escalation, on the row of the layer that ruled: the passed-up objection ids one of its seats sustained (the layer counts as objecting).

floor_by.description: Additive. `request`: on the rows of a pass that was asked to start at layer 3 by a request (--next-pass-layer-3, then a routed decision of `council route-decide` in the gate ledger) rather than by the ladder's own count; the re-ask of such a pass after a layer-3 judge was not heard carries it too. `ladder`: only on a row that was not asked because the ladder started the pass above that layer. `ladder_visits`: only on the row of a layer that the ladder passed over because the layer had used its visits.

escalated_by.description: 0.8.4, additive, present only on a layer row with state escalated that was left unasked because the person sent the plan up (--send-up), because layer 1 had used its revisions and the plan went up to layer 2 (layer1_bound), or because layer 2 had used its revisions and the plan went up to layer 3 (layer2_bound); a stall escalation leaves it out.

raised_again.description: Stall escalation, after the floor reset: ids a judge of this layer raised again although a ruling had closed them or given them to another judge; see escalations[].raised_again for whether each one counts.

layer_one_open.description: Present only on a row of a layer between the first and the top one that was shown layer 1's open objections with the rating in force (once the judges rate their objections, on a layered chain with answer_back): how many objections the section listed (shown), how many lower-rated ones were left out because the section would pass the objection ledger's own size budget (left_out), and the size of the section as sent (chars, and tokens_est = an estimate from UTF-8 bytes / 4). Additive (0.8.4): not_shown is present only when this layer was shown the section it rules on and left_out is above 0: the ids of the objections the size budget left out, which are not ruled on and stay open as they were. Counts and ids only: the text is in the stage prompt, never copied here. Experimental.

rulings_in_call.description: Additive (0.8.4), present only on the row of the second layer when, in its ordinary review, it was shown layer 1's open objections to rule on and at least one could be ruled on: one entry per objection it was asked to rule on. outcome is sustained (one or more judges of the layer sustained it; adopted_as gives the new id each of them holds it under), overruled (every judge of the layer overruled it) or undecided (no ruling settled it, also when no judge gave a usable ruling; why says why). stays_open is on an overruled entry only, computed when the report is written from the rating in force then: false = the overrule closed it, true = it stays open (rated 4 or above, not rated, or once rated 7 or above). rated is the rating the ruling was judged on (null = not rated, which counts as 4 or above). by lists each judge's ruling and its reason (model-supplied text), or why that judge gave none. Experimental.

ledger.description: Present only on a row of the TOP layer that was shown the objection ledger (a layered chain with answer_back): how many objection rows the section held (rows), how many were open (active), how many closed ones were left out (closed_cut), and the size of the section as sent (chars, and tokens_est = an estimate from UTF-8 bytes / 4 that under-counts non-Latin text). Counts only: the text is in the stage prompt, never copied here.

carried.description: Seats of this layer whose verdict is carried from an earlier round on the same unchanged draft (no new call, no new charge).

layers.description: 0.8.3, present only on a layered chain (seats.critics[].layer): one row per round per layer, in layer order. A layer that was not asked in a round is a row with state not_asked, never an absent row. signoff[] and panelVerdicts[] list asked seats only; this is where the layers that were not asked are recorded.

review_notes.description: 0.8.3 notes lane, present only when the chain's reviewNotes switch was on and the lane ran. Each judge's capped proposals and improvement ideas, as the judge wrote them (quoted model text; they decide nothing in the plan): the items kept within the per-round cap with who raised the same exact text in the same overseer round (raised_by), what was cut for the per-round cap (cut), the replies whose notes were not read and why (dropped), and how many items were longer than the length the judge was asked to keep (long). Each item's attempt names the stage file that holds the reply it came from: an empty string for the judge's first reply of the pass, otherwise the suffix of that file's label (for example reask1, reask2, answered, retry). A seat's items from every reply of a pass are read when the seat ends the pass with a verdict; counted in dropped instead are the replies of a seat that ends it unheard (verdict_not_recorded), replies a provider cut off or ended early (reply_cut_off, reply_incomplete) and an id the judge already gave in an earlier reply of the same pass (duplicate_of_earlier_reply). Each item's answer is what the writer replied, recorded as it was given (status taken, declined, same, unanswered, conflicting or builder_task) and the stage that carried it (from); the writer's claim is not checked. answers_from lists the stages that carried answers, as stage labels (revise-N, revise-N-full, handoff, notes-answer); answer.ending, on an answer given after the panel ended (handoff, notes-answer), names how the panel ended (signed_off, finish_chosen, layer_stop, no_reviewer_heard, not_quorate, not_signed_off); answer_counts counts what the writer wrote that did not become an answer (a line naming no item, a SAME with no valid target, malformed, repeated or reasonless lines, and a later different answer for an id already answered).

proposer_returns.description: One row for each objection of the top layer that said it was about a decision (not about wording), written by chains that have the Decisions rule on and nothing otherwise. A row says which overseer round and pass it ended, which Decisions entry was contested (number, title, the Choice line that was quoted), the objection and the criterion it cites, and what the run did: route proposers (the decision went back to the proposers: the alternative, the post and the answer read from each, an unreadable one with its reason) or route writer (no proposer seat, or a mark that could not be checked against the plan's text; status refused says why). The seat that raised the objection is not named.

overseer_round.description: The overseer round the objection ended.

pass.description: The review pass in which the top layer objected.

route.description: proposers: the decision went back to the proposers; writer: it went to the writer.

status.description: ran: the return was made; failed: no alternative could be read, so the objection went to the writer as an ordinary one; no_proposers: the chain has no proposer seat; refused: the mark was not taken as a decision-level objection (see refused).

entry.description: The number of the contested Decisions entry.

selected_by.description: named: the top layer named it as the most consequential; majority: more seats named it; first_listed: the first the seat listed; first_recorded: the first in the objection ledger.

refused.description: Why the mark was not taken as a decision-level objection (status refused).

alternatives.description: One entry per proposer: the alternative it wrote.

posts.description: The posts written on the others' alternatives.

calls.description: The calls the return made (at most three per proposer).

writer_step.description: The revise stage that carried the result to the writer.

pass.description: The review pass in which the conflict was found.

label.description: The decider stage's label (conflict-<pass>), absent when no call was made.

kind.description: external: the decider is the person's session (the run pauses for its answer); seat: a paid seat; none: the chain names no decider.

shares_lab_with.description: The labs of the conflict that the decider's own lab equals: a ruling by one of the two sides is visible.

ids.description: The objection that came back first, then the objections fixed in between.

overseer_round.description: Present only on a chain with overseer rounds: the overseer round this pass belongs to.

rounds.description: Parallel to ids: the pass each objection was raised in.

silent_round.description: The pass in which the first objection's judge was asked and did not list it (the evidence for the swing).

prevail.description: An id from ids, or "neither". A ruling annotates; it never closes an objection.

why.description: Present when decided is false: why nobody ruled; escalated (stall escalation, a closed enum widened): the pass that found the swing stalled and its objections were passed up a layer instead of going to the decider; person_asked: the decider asked for the person and the run stopped for the answer. Present with decided true on tree_member: the ask is not offered to a tree member, so the applied side is neither.

via.description: Present when the person chose (the channel: cli); no actor is claimed.

decider_prevail.description: What the decider leaned to when it asked for the person (or when the applied side is not its own).

decisions.description: 0.8.3 E4b, additive, present only when the layered panel found a conflict (an objection from a judge of one layer came back after the writer revised the plan in response to an objection from another layer): one row per conflict, with the ruling or the reason nobody ruled.

overseer_rounds.description: 0.8.3, present only on a chain with overseer rounds: how many overseer rounds are complete (the top layer gave a verdict in each).

escalations.description: Stall escalation (0.8.4), present only when a stall below the top layer was passed up a layer instead of ending the run: one row per escalation. In the stalled pass (`round`) the writer did not revise the plan; in `pass` the layers from `to_layer` up were asked, and right after its blind review each seat of `to_layer` ruled on the stuck objections (stage rule-<pass>-<seat>). A sustained objection became the sustaining seat's own (adopted_as); an overruled one is closed although its raiser did not withdraw it only when it is rated below 4 (and was never rated 7 or above), and otherwise stays open under its id (see stays_open in outcome) (a later re-raise of its id is recorded in raised_again, which says whether it counts); an undecided one stays standing as its raiser's.

round.description: The pass in which the stall fired.

pass.description: The pass in which the plan was passed up and ruled on.

from_layer.description: The highest layer among the labs whose objections make up the stall (the objections the stall rule counted, each standing unchanged through the stall window of its judge's verdicts).

trigger.description: Why the plan was passed up (0.8.4, additive): stall = the stall rule (an objection that stood unchanged through the stall window of its judge's verdicts); send_up = the person sent layer 1's open objections up at a layer-1 revision-bound stop (--send-up); layer1_bound = layer 1 had used its revisions in an overseer round and objected again, so layer 1's open objections went up to layer 2 instead of the run stopping; no revision was used; layer2_bound = layer 2 had used its revisions in an overseer round and objected again, so layer 2's open objections went up to layer 3 instead of the run stopping; no revision was used.

seats.description: Additive (0.8.4, same-layer seats): the seat keys of the raisers, present when a key differs from its lab.

stalled.description: Additive (0.8.4): for a stall escalation, the objections that reached the stall window, each with the passes in which it stood (the window is the chain's dispute.stall_rounds). Absent for a send-up, which passes up every open objection.

seat.description: Additive (0.8.4, same-layer seats): the seat key of the raiser, present when it differs from the lab (a model that sits more than once in the panel).

unresolved_at_bound.description: Additive (0.8.4). Only on a layer1_bound row, and only when there are any: the ids, among those that went up, whose outcome in the exchange of the pass that reached layer 1's bound was unresolved_at_stop (still changing when that exchange stopped at its last round).

not_debated.description: Additive (0.8.4): the passed-up objections that the exchange of the layer that raised them left not debated. They climb flagged and are NOT ruled on (no ruling, no overrule can close one); they stay standing. `next` says what became of each, derived from the record when the report is written: debated_after_send_back (a later pass's exchange has a row for it that is no longer not_debated and drew a post), withdrawn (its raiser withdrew it in an answer after the climb), standing_dissent (the run ended at the escalated sign-off with it still standing), pending (the run stopped before any of these).

seat.description: Additive (0.8.4, same-layer seats): the seat key of the raiser, present when it differs from the lab.

layer.description: Present only when the layer that left the objection not debated is not the lowest (the shortened exchange of an upper layer).

why.description: Why there is no ruling: prompt_held, ruler_unreachable, unreadable_ruling, unknown_id, overrule_without_reason, conflicting_rulings, no_ruling.

raised_again.description: After the floor reset: the raiser raised an id again that this escalation's ruling had closed or moved. A quoted re-raise is recorded and not counted; an unquoted one (counted: true) is a live objection again, since its id cannot tell it from another problem under the same criterion.

problem.description: The raiser's words for the objection (model text).

rated.description: The rating the ruling was judged on (0.8.4, additive): null = not rated at the ruling (an objection that is not rated counts as 4 or above). For a sustained row it is the rating the adopted copy carries over from the original: the sustaining seat gave none. Absent in a report written before 0.8.4.

reasons_shown_in.description: Additive (0.8.4), only on an overruled row of a ruling made by the top layer: the round in which the judge that raised the objection was first shown the top layer's reasons for it, in that judge's next review after the top layer objected and the plan went back to be revised. Absent otherwise, for example when the top layer signed off, the overrule closed the objection, the judge withdrew it first, or the judge's next review did not come.

stays_open.description: Only on an overruled row (0.8.4, additive): true = the objection stays open under its id (rated 4 or above, not rated, or once rated 7 or above); false = the overrule closed it. Computed when the report is written, from the rating in force then, so a handler's later re-tag below 4 shows as false. Absent on a sustained or undecided row and in a report written before 0.8.4: read as closed, as before.

withdrawn_in_exchange.description: True only when this seat withdrew the same objection (same id) in its layer's exchange in the same pass: the later act counts, so the sustain made it the seat's own again, and both acts are on the record (the exchange row says it was withdrawn, this entry says it was taken over).

handler_retags.description: Additive, present only when the handler session changed an objection's rating, or a late finding's rating at the build check, during the run with `council retag-add`: one row per re-tag, oldest first, with the pass it applies from, the objection id, the new rating, the reason, who made it (`handler`) and when. A re-tag is the handler session's own act and needs no answer from the person; the change of the rating itself (old and new rating) is in `severity.retags`, where a re-tag that could not be applied is in `severity.retags_refused`. A re-tag for a pass that never ran is listed here only.

handler_notes.description: Additive, present only after the handling session added a note to the build list once the run had ended, with `council note-add`: one row per note, oldest first (n, at, actor "handler", text, and objection when the note names one). A note is the handler's own text, never a seat's, and it sorts nothing: the objections of the run stay as they were. The notes are also in HANDOFF.md, in one section before the criteria lock block.

owner_rulings.description: Additive, present only when the person who owns the request gave rulings during the run: one row per approved ruling, oldest first, with the pass it applies from, the ruling as it was shown to the person and, when the handler session relayed it, the person's answer as quoted.

withdrawn.description: Present when the person took this ruling out of force from a later pass on. The ruling stays in the record: the passes before from_pass carried it.

declined_requests.description: Additive, present only when the handler session declined a request it had asked for (a ruling or a withdrawal the person never answered). Such a request set nothing, so it has no person_words and is not in `relayed`; the gate ledger holds the same line.

relayed.description: Additive, present only when the handler session relayed an answer on a person's permission (`council relay-answer`, or a choice at a stop through the stop_decide tool, kind stop_decision): one row per relayed answer, oldest first, with the person's words as the handler quoted them. The tool cannot verify the permission; the record shows who relayed it.

cap_name.description: 0.8.4: the per-provider cap a relayed raise was for (COUNCIL_SPEND_CAPS); absent otherwise.

not_taken.description: 0.8.4: present when the harness closed this answer because the run did not take it (the command line refused its number, or the resume did not start). The answer is on the ledger and is not a choice the run made.

run_controls.description: Additive, present only when the run has a request or a decision to start a pass at layer 3 (`--next-pass-layer-3`, then `council route-decide`): one row per request, or per route the handler made without a request, oldest first, read from the gate ledger when the report is written. `request` is null for a route the handler or the person decided with no request; `decision` is null for a request nobody has decided (it stays listed, also after its pass has run, and is never closed by the harness). request.channel is cli (typed at a terminal) or session (relayed by the handler session, with the person's words in person_words; request.reason then holds the relay sentence). decision.decided_by is handler (the handler session decided, with its own reason) or person (the person decided and the handler carried the answer out: person_words holds the person's answer as typed and reason is the relay sentence; the tool cannot verify the permission). `at` is the ledger's own time.

reason.description: Present only when channel is session, and derived from the channel alone when the report is written (the request line records no reason): the relay sentence, the same one a decision that is the person's and a relayed raise carry.

pauses.description: Additive, present only when someone asked the running run to pause after the pass in progress (`council pause`, 0.8.4): one row per request, oldest first, read from the gate ledger when the report is written. `pass` is the pass the run was in when it was asked. `request` says who asked: `by` person (`channel` cli: typed at the terminal; `channel` session: the handler session relayed the person's answer, in `person_words`) or handler (`reason` is its own, MODEL-SUPPLIED: a claim). `taken` is set when the resume continued the run from the pause it caused (`seq`, `at`); `lapsed` when the request ended without a pause, because the run went on or ended some other way first. A request with neither was never reached (the last pass was running, or the chain has no later pass) and stays listed.

lapsed.description: A request that never paused the run (the sitting it was asked of ended some other way). Not a pause that was finished: see `finished`.

pass.description: The pass the pause stopped before.

finished.description: 0.8.4: the run DID pause for this request and the person ended it there (finish: the closing steps and, on a layered chain, the final read; finish_now: no judge asked again). `taken` is a pause that was resumed; `lapsed` a request that never paused the run; exactly one of the three is set once the request is settled.

raises.description: Additive, present only when the run USED a raise of its typed spending limit (a raise the run set aside or never used is not listed): one row per raise, oldest first, read from the gate ledger when the report is written. old_usd is the total of the same cap that was in force before (null: none recorded before), new_usd the total that replaced it. channel is the ledger's own value: cli (typed at a terminal), elicitation (typed in a dialog of an MCP client; client_name and client_version are the client's own words about itself) or session (relayed by the handler session on the person's permission, with the person's words in person_words; the tool cannot verify the permission). actor is the user name, the client's name or main-session; cap_name is present under the per-provider caps.

dissents.description: Additive (0.8.4). Present only when the run ended at the top layer's sign-off and an open objection of a lower-layer judge was overruled by that layer without being closed (rated 4 or above, not rated, or once rated 7 or above): one entry per such objection, a dissent. A dissent is not a signature: the judge's layer is neither signed nor blocking. It is never in report-partial.json. Each entry names the judge (its name, seat and lab), the objection (id, criterion, problem and quoted passage: model-supplied text), its rating as raised, in force at the end, and every change of it with the pass and who made it (layer3 or handler), the top layer's ruling (layer, round, and each judge's reasons: model-supplied text), and kept: the round of the judge's latest answer that kept the objection after the top layer overruled it, with its reason when it gave one (model-supplied text); absent when it did not answer after the overrule. Its status is open.

acceptance.description: 0.8.4: present only when a person or the handling session accepted the plan of a run that ended without agreement, as it stands (council accept, or step accept of stop_decide), after the run ended. It is a copy derived from the gate ledger, which is the authority. It agrees with no judge and changes no objection: the ending word, the banner and every open objection stay. gate: the ledger's gate; actor and channel: who answered and where (cli for the terminal, session for the handling session; a person's acceptance relayed by the session is actor person, channel session, relayed true, with the person's words in person_words and the relay sentence as the reason); at, reason: when and why, in the acceptor's words; advisor, advisor_said: for the session, its advisor's state and words; objections: the open objections and the late findings (late: true, ids starting L-) accepted as they stand, each with the session's person test for it when the session accepted; over_disagreement: the ids on which the session and its advisor differed; status_restored: the Status word the handoff seat wrote, when the harness had replaced it with needs_decision and the acceptance gave it back.

ending_word.description: 0.8.4: ONE word for how this run ended, on every run that has a report (a run that waits at a stop has none: it has no report.json). The words are signed_off, signed_off_at_top_not_agreed, escalated_signoff, early_finish, rule_no_handler, finish_chosen, layer_stop, no_reviewer_heard, not_quorate, stalled and round_cap. It relates to the two older records by the one question they all answer, agreed or not agreed, not by vocabulary. `final_read.run_end` is the reading before the final read: agreed when the panel passed or the handler said good to build; a final read that objects turns that into not agreed. `ending` (how the top layer's sign-off ended) says agreed or not agreed for the run it is on. A signed_off run is agreed when it passed and no final read blocks it, or when `ending` says agreed; an escalated_signoff or finish_chosen run is agreed only when `ending` says so; every other word is never agreed. `dispute.reason` is a copy derived from this word in its older spelling (panel_signed_off, layer_not_signed_off, no_heard_reviewer), and `no_open_objections` there stands for a stalled or capped end with no open objection. Absent in a report written before this field existed.

stop_kind.description: 0.8.4: on a run whose `ending_word` is finish_chosen or rule_no_handler, the kind of the stop it ended at: the stop's `kind`, with `/<why>` when the stop has a why (layer_bound/revisions, layer_bound/unheard, layer_bound/final_read, overseer_cap, stall_stop/top_layer, stall_stop/last_pass, stall_stop/climb_not_shown, stall_stop/ladder_next, secret_pause, budget_stop). A hard stop (seven or more overseer rounds) is not a kind of its own: read `stop.rounds`. A run on the ladder has no layer-3 count and so no hard stop: its stall stop carries no `rounds` field, and `stop.overseer_round` says which overseer round it was in. Absent when the run did not end at a stop.

ending.description: 0.8.4: how the top layer's sign-off ended on a layered run, present only when the run ended at that sign-off (a run that went on or ended otherwise after a build check that sent the plan back has none). `passed` is never set by it. kind agreed: the top layer signed off (and no final read objects, on a chain that has one), and either the handler answered good_to_build to the build check, on the very plan the top layer signed (signed_sha), or there is no handling session, so no build check was made (basis no_handling_session, handler_check none; a sign-off that every layer gave); an escalated sign-off that the handler agreed is agreed with `passed` false. kind signed_off_at_top_not_agreed: the top layer signed off and the run does NOT end agreed: the handler answered not_yet and the run ended there (handler_not_yet), or the plan delivered is not the one the top layer signed (text_changed_after_sign_off; with no handling session a changed plan that the final read ran on and every top-layer seat cleared counts as signed), or an objection to the final plan holds (final_read_objection). A ladder or an escalated sign-off with no handling session has no ending: it is not agreement of the whole panel (`passed` false). The exit code, `outcome`, the verdict line, the BOARD banner and run_status read it. A run that waits at the build check has no report.json (it is paused: NEEDS-build-check-<n>.md); a stop is a report-partial.json. The mark dissent_on_record is added to basis when the report holds dissents (see `dissents`).

handler_check.description: What the handler answered to the last build check; none when no check was asked (no handling session).

signed_sha.description: The 12-hex id of the plan the top layer signed (the same id the final read and the answer envelopes use).

pass.description: The pass in which the top layer signed off.

refused_answers.description: Answers to the build check that were set aside (refused for not naming every open objection, or stale), counted by listing superseded/ in the run folder, never a counter.

build_check_refusals.description: 0.8.4, additive: every refused answer of the run's handler pauses, named by label (build-check-<n>, sort-<n>), in order, derived from the run folder (superseded/), never counted anywhere else. A refused answer is not a build check: it is set aside and the run waits again, so it is not a row of build_checks. Each row: n and label (the check), pass, why (unreadable: the answer was neither good_to_build nor not_yet; no_reasons: a not_yet without reasons; ids_missing: the answer did not name every id it had to name), missing (the ids it did not name; empty unless ids_missing) and required (the ids it had to name). It also holds the refused answers of the handler's sort wait (label sort-<n>); an n of 1 can mean build-check-1 or sort-1, and label tells them apart.

build_checks.description: 0.8.4: every build check the run asked, in order, whatever the run's ending: the handler's answer to each top-layer sign-off (a not_yet that sent the plan back for a revision is a row here although the run ended later, and the run may then have no `ending`). Present only when the chain has a handling session and the run reached a top-layer sign-off.

kind.description: full: every layer signed in the pass; ladder: a ladder sign-off; escalated: an escalated sign-off (an objection was passed up).

required.description: The ids the answer had to name: the open objection ids (every open objection, below 4 included) and the id of every late finding (L-...), whatever its rating, except a late finding made from an unanchored failure that is itself required: that pair is named once, and either id satisfies it.

escalated_signoff.description: Stall escalation: the ending in which every layer the climb asked signed off, the top layer included, while the layers in `below` were passed over. It is NOT consensus: `passed` stays false (the judges below did not sign off) and `outcome` is not widened; the dispute stage runs over the standing passed-up objections (unless the handler then answered good_to_build to the build check: nothing changes the plan after that, and `dispute` records `ran: false` with this reason). A pass that the handler's routed decision (`--next-pass-layer-3`) started at layer 3 on a chain without the ladder ends the same way: `requested` is true, `ladder` is absent, `below` lists the layers that were not asked, and nothing was passed up.
