A sign-off under the ladder is recorded here too: `ladder` is true, `below` lists the layers that were not asked in that pass, no stall happened and nothing was passed up.

requested.description: Additive: present (true) when the pass that ended the run was asked to start at layer 3 by a request (--next-pass-layer-3), not by the ladder's own count.

ladder.description: Present (true) when the run ran under the ladder (run.json `ladder`) and the top layer signed off in a pass that did not ask every layer: `below` lists the layers that were not asked in that pass.

raised_again.description: Present when the sign-off came while a judge still raised ids a ruling had closed (see escalations[].raised_again); below is then empty.

kind.description: budget_stop (0.8.4, a closed enum widened: a reader that validates `kind` strictly must accept it): the person chose --finish at the spending limit; the run ended not agreed after the final read, before the stage in `label` was paid for. `cap_name` names the cap when per-provider caps were armed. overseer_cap and layer_bound: a limit the run stopped at. stall_stop (0.8.4, a closed enum widened: a reader that validates kind strictly must accept it): objections stood unchanged through the stall window of their judges' verdicts and cannot be passed up (the top layer holds one; no pass is left; the chain keeps no answer-back list or does not ask its judges to rate; or the next pass is a ladder pass, which does not pass a plan up); `why`, `top_layer` and `stalled` say which; the run is resumable and the person chooses to continue (only while a pass is left, see `pass_left`: the stalled objections are counted afresh and no overseer round is added) or to finish; from seven used overseer rounds (`rounds`) it presents as the hard stop (only the person decides there; the same choices are offered). owner_pause (0.8.4, a closed enum widened): the person or the handler session asked the running run to pause between two passes (`council pause`) and it stopped before pass `pass` started; `request_seq` names the ledger request; it is resumable by a plain `council --resume`, exits 23, and is NOT a limit. early_finish (added in 0.8.3, a closed enum widened: a reader that validates kind strictly must accept it): the run FINISHED early at the session's proposal with the overseer layer's yes; it is NOT agreement (passed false, outcome not widened, exit 22). secret_pause (0.8.4, a closed enum widened): the run was paused at a credential-shaped string in a prompt, the person chose --finish and then --continue, and the pass loop ended at the paused stage (`label`) instead of asking it; the ordinary not-agreed ending ran after it. The report carries `stop` in this case on any chain, layered or not.

why.description: layer_bound: `revisions` = the layer used all the revisions it is allowed in one overseer round, `unheard` = a seat of it stayed silent for too many passes in a row. stall_stop (0.8.4): `top_layer` = the top layer holds at least one of the stalled objections, `last_pass` = it holds none and no pass is left, `climb_not_shown` = a pass is left but the stall is not passed up because the chain does not keep the answer-back list or its judges are not asked to rate (the layer above would not be shown the climb), `ladder_next` = the next pass is a ladder pass, which does not pass a plan up. layer_bound (0.8.4): `final_read` = no seat of the top layer gave a usable reply to the final read, so nobody has read the final plan; the run stopped there, resumable, and ends only after a read.

top_layer.description: stall_stop and layer_bound final_read only (0.8.4): the number of the chain's top layer.

attempt.description: layer_bound final_read only (0.8.4): 0 at the first stop; each continue that reads again and finds nobody makes the next stop one higher.

no_chooser.description: layer_bound final_read only (0.8.4): true when the run has no handling session, so the stop is a pause that names nobody to choose.

finish_read_used.description: layer_bound final_read only (0.8.4): true once the one final read before a finish has been made in this run.

finish_refused.description: layer_bound final_read only (0.8.4): present when a finish was asked for while no seat had read: `ran` = the final read before it ran and found nobody, `repeat` = the request was answered from the record with no read.

pass_left.description: stall_stop only (0.8.4): whether a pass is left. false = --continue is refused (no pass is left to go on with); --finish stays.

seat.description: Additive (0.8.4, same-layer seats): the seat key of the raiser, present when it differs from the lab.

stalled.description: 0.8.4, additive: the objections that stood unchanged through the stall window when this stop was raised (the same shape as escalations[].stalled). On stall_stop always; on an overseer_cap stop only when a top-layer stall was pending at it.

rounds.description: overseer_cap, and stall_stop on a chain without the ladder: the overseer round the stop was in (on a ladder run's overseer_cap: the top-layer reads made); seven or more makes it the hard stop, except on a ladder run (`ladder`: true). Absent on a ladder run's stall stop: a ladder has no layer-3 count and no hard stop (`overseer_round` still says which round).

handler_not_yet.description: 0.8.4, overseer_cap only: the stop was reached by the handler's not_yet at the build check (it counts as a top-layer objection for the overseer rounds), not by a judge's objection.

label.description: kind secret_pause: the stage that was paused at a credential-shaped string when the person chose --finish. kind budget_stop: the stage the spending limit stopped before it was paid for.

phase.description: 0.8.4: kind budget_stop in a STOPPED run's report-partial.json: where in the run the spending limit stopped it (before the review rounds, inside them, after them). The stop is the person's alone to answer.

cap_name.description: kind budget_stop only (0.8.4): the name of the spend cap that stopped the run, when per-provider caps were armed (the name STOPPED-budget.json carries as capName).

reviewed.description: kind secret_pause only: how much of the pass the loop ended in was asked: none (nothing answered or cut, or an unlayered panel that did not finish), part (some layers answered, cut off or not asked; see asked_layers, cut_layers, not_asked_layers), all (every layer answered, or an unlayered panel recorded; the finish came at the decider, the revise or the allocator) or signed (every layer of the pass signed off and the finish came at the handler's build check).

asked_layers.description: kind secret_pause on a layered chain: the layers answered in the pass the loop ended in.

cut_layers.description: kind secret_pause on a layered chain: the layers whose call or settling call was cut off by the finish (state unfinished in layers[]); their seats' replies stay in panelVerdicts[] and signoff[] marked cut and count for no sign-off, no read and no open objection of their own (a ruling the layer completed before the cut stands).

not_asked_layers.description: kind secret_pause on a layered chain: the layers of that pass that were never reached; they stay not_asked in layers[].

request_seq.description: owner_pause only: the seq of the `pause_requested` line of the gate ledger the run stopped for.

reason.description: early_finish only. MODEL-SUPPLIED: the session's own written reason, as it wrote it (cut at 1000 characters). A claim, not a finding.

earlier.description: 0.8.4, additive: true only on an objection that stands from an earlier pass, one that nobody has closed and that the pass which triggered the revise did not raise again. Its `handled` is open, because what the revise did with it is not recorded.

declined_reason.description: Present only when handled is declined: the reason the reviser gave for declining this objection, as it wrote it (cut at 600 characters). MODEL-SUPPLIED: a claim, not a finding.

items.description: early_finish only. Every objection open in the record when the session proposed to finish, derived from the record (never from the session's words). For an objection of the pass that triggered the revise, `handled` says what the revise did: declined with a reason, changed, unchanged, or open (the chain records no objection ids). An objection that stands from an earlier pass is listed with `handled` open and `earlier` true. This is the list the overseer layer was asked about, and the list handed to the builder as tasks.

overseer.description: early_finish only: the labs of the overseer layer that said yes.

overseer_seats.description: early_finish only, additive: the seat keys of the overseer layer that said yes, present when a seat's key differs from its lab (one model on several layers or twice on one layer).

ladder.description: 0.8.4: present (true) on an overseer_cap or stall_stop of a run with the ladder in force. An overseer_cap so marked is the stop at the limit the person typed (--rounds N): it is the person's alone at every N. Neither kind is ever the seven-round hard stop.

relayed.description: 0.8.4: present (true) when the finish that ended the run (finish or finish-now) was the person's own words relayed by the handling session (the run.json choice and the gate ledger carry the words).

finished_at_once.description: 0.8.4: present (true) when the person chose finish-now at this stop: `chosen` stays finish, and the run ended with no ending exchange and no judge asked again: no final read was made at this finish (final_read.reason says whether the top layer had already read this text), except that a final read already on disk for this text is kept and counts as read (final_read.seats[]); at the final-read stop itself (why final_read) the final read was asked before the person finished and no seat gave a usable reply, and none is asked again.

chosen.description: `rule` (0.8.4): the run has no handling session, so nobody could choose at the stop kept here and the run ended there, not agreed; nobody chose it. `early` (kind early_finish only): the run ended at the session's proposal and the overseer layer's yes, nobody chose it at a limit. `finish`: Present only when the person ended the stopped run with --finish: the run then finished as not agreed and the stop is kept in report.json with this field. A stop that is still waiting for the person's choice has no `chosen`.

stop.description: 0.8.3. Three shapes, all NOT agreement. (1) kind overseer_cap, layer_bound or stall_stop: present in report-partial.json of a layered run that stopped at the overseer-round cap, at a layer's bound or at a stall that cannot be passed up (`why` says which for layer_bound and stall_stop: the layer used all the revisions it is allowed in one overseer round, or a seat of it stayed silent for too many passes in a row; or the top layer holds a stalled objection, or no pass is left, or the chain keeps no answer-back list or does not ask its judges to rate, or the next pass is a ladder pass, which does not pass a plan up); the run is resumable and the person chooses to continue or to finish; present in report.json of such a run once the person finished it with --finish (then with `chosen: finish`). (2) kind early_finish: report.json ONLY (never report-partial; the run is not resumable, it finished) of a layered run whose session reviser proposed to finish early and whose overseer layer said yes (`chosen: early`); passed is false and exit 22 follows. (3) kind overseer_cap or layer_bound with `chosen: rule` (0.8.4): report.json ONLY, of a layered run that has no handling session and that ended at the overseer-round limit (not the hard stop) or at a silent seat of layer 1 or 2 instead of stopping; nobody chose it; passed is false and exit 22 follows. Never in report.json of a run that neither stopped nor finished early.

ledger.description: With reason ledger_overflow: the size of the objection ledger that did not fit (the open objections alone exceeded the budget), so nothing was sent to the top layer.

layerStop.description: 0.8.3, present only when a layered run stopped because a layer ended it with no objection and no usable vote: nobody in the layer gave a verdict (only_stated_passes), a seat of the top layer stated a pass instead of signing off (top_layer_not_explicit; labs names them), or there was nothing to revise against (no_objection_to_revise). Not agreement: passed is false.

heard.description: Reviewers that gave a verdict (signed off or objected) that round.

passedOnly.description: Reviewers that only stated a pass.

notQuorate.description: Since 0.7.8. Present only when the chain sets quorum.minHeard and a review round in which every verdict was a sign-off had fewer verdicts than that; the loop stopped there. Not agreement: passed is false and outcome is 'degraded'.

answered_under_earlier_wording.description: Added in 0.8.4. Present only when the run was resumed after an update of THC changed a prompt sentence and some saved stages were kept as they were instead of being asked again: each row names the stage, its pass when it has one, the cause ('prompt': the only cause kept) and the version of THC that wrote it. Rebuilt in every sitting; a stage whose prompt changed because something it depends on changed is asked again and is not listed.

answered_on_another_route.description: Added in 0.8.4. Present only when the run was resumed on another route (the direct Anthropic key, OpenRouter, or a Claude Code session) and some saved stages were kept as they were instead of being asked again: each row names the stage, its pass when it has one, the route it was written on and the route of this sitting ('anthropic', 'openrouter' or 'session'). Rebuilt in every sitting; a stage whose prompt changed because something it depends on changed is asked again and is not listed.

unverifiedReplays.description: Present only when some stage was replayed from the stage cache but could be checked only against the task and chain, not the exact prompt.

argued.description: Present only on chains with argued.enabled: where the 'How this plan was argued' text is, and the check of every id and lab it names against this run's record.

criteria_sha256.description: sha256 over the criteria list, each criterion collapsed to one line, order counted (0.8.0). The same fingerprint the HANDOFF.md lock block carries; `council check-lock` compares them.

field_cuts.description: Every model-written field the harness cut before the next stages read it (0.8.1): a whole architecture's field, a debate post or reply longer than its seat's own token cap allowed (at least 40,000 characters), or a critic field over 8,000 characters. One row per cut, also written to WARNINGS.md. Absent when nothing was cut; absent on reports written before 0.8.1, which cut at 2,000 characters without a record.

stage.description: The stage whose reply held the field, when known.

checks_sha256.description: sha256 over how each criterion is checked, index-aligned with `criteria`: for a checkable criterion its `check` and `on` (from `criteria_kinds`), null for every other one, order counted (0.8.1). criteria_sha256 covers the wording only, so an edited check changes this and not that. The HANDOFF.md lock block carries the same hash in its second marker (`the-high-council:criteria-checks`); `council check-lock` compares them. Absent on reports written before 0.8.1.

criteria_lints.description: Word-level lints over the acceptance criteria, run before any paid review round (0.8.0). Heuristics: they miss a rephrasing and can flag a good criterion. Recorded only: never a stop. [] when clean.

signoff_table_gaps.description: Sign-offs refused because the per-criterion table was not full (a row for every criterion, each with evidence and a verdict that says MET or FAILED), on a chain with signoff_table.required. Present only when there was one. The seat counted as unheard (an abstention), never as consent. Added in 0.8.2.

outside_criteria_rows.description: Table rows a reply carried that named none of the criteria (ticket 16): recorded, never counted for or against any seat. Present only when there were some. Added in 0.8.2.

layer_debates.description: Additive, present only when a layer exchange ran or was due and could not run (a row with `not_run`; with the shortened exchange of the layers above the lowest, such a row can be at any layer): per pass and layer, the rounds and each objection with its posts, the raiser's answers and the outcome (and, where the judges rate their objections, the objection's severity, recorded here only: the exchange never shows a rating to the judges). Written since 0.8.4's exchange; declared here so a reader can rely on its shape being named.

not_run.description: Present only when the exchange could not run in this pass because fewer than two judges of the layer were heard (a layer of one seat included); the objections that stood are listed, flagged not_debated, and where a judge was unheard it is asked again on the same draft.

signoffs.description: Present only in the shortened exchange of a layer above the lowest: for each raiser that replied, the sign-off line its reply ended with (`line`: yes, no, missing or garbled) and the JSON field `sign_off` (`field`, the same words); what it said (`said`: yes, no, or null when neither was readable; no when the two differ); whether the two differ (`differs`); what the computed rule makes of its verdict after the exchange (`computed`: signs, objects or unheard); and whether what it said goes against that (`against_computed`). Record only.

re_asked.description: Present only at the top layer, when this raiser's reply ended with `sign-off: no` while no objection of its own rated 4 or above (or without a rating) still stood: the seat was asked once more for its verdict. `result`: signs (a clean verdict), objects (it named an objection, listed in `objections`; `re_raised` names those it had withdrawn in this pass's exchange; a stated pass that still holds objections of its own also reads objects, with none listed), unheard (a verdict that could not be read, or, where the judges are asked to rate, a verdict that names no objection: left to the layer's unheard handling) or stated_pass (it stated a pass: heard, no sign-off given and no objection named; it is not counted as signing off).

safety_stop.description: True when the exchange ran every round its budget allowed (seven at most) and the last round still changed something and an objection still stands after it; the objections still changing in it are unresolved_at_stop. Absent otherwise (also when everything was withdrawn in the last round).

proposed.description: A defect a judge named in an exchange post that cannot become an objection, with the reason (`why`): no_criterion (it names no criterion; recorded on every layered chain) or no_valid_rating (it carries no valid rating; recorded only when the rating demand is in force). It is recorded here and nowhere else: no id is minted, it is not an objection and holds nothing, nobody is asked again, and the rest of the post counts. One entry per post and round.

criterion.description: Absent when the reason is no_criterion.

carried_from.description: Present only on an objection an earlier pass's exchange did not reach (raised or amended in its last round): the pass that carried it. It is debated from round 1 of this pass.

outcome.description: How the objection ended in the exchange: withdrawn_argued (its raiser withdrew with a reason), stands_uncontested (standing, and no reviewer's latest position on its final text is a contest or insufficient evidence), stands_contested (standing, and at least one reviewer's latest position there is one), not_debated (no round followed its raising or amending) or unresolved_at_stop (still changing when the exchange stopped at the last round its budget allows). A reviewer's latest position is its latest counted post: an explicit no_view is a position that is neither, and an omitted or refused post is not a position.

minority_notes.description: Per objection, verbatim from the judges' posts: the contest reasons when the objection stands, the support reasons when its raiser withdrew it. One entry per judge, from that judge's latest counted post.

omitted.description: Present only when a judge shown this objection left no post on it (its reply could not be read, its call failed, or it skipped the objection): one entry per judge and round, with the reason (omitted, unreadable or no_reply). Counts as no view in that round; in a later round the judge's earlier position is carried forward as a flagged post instead.

posts.description: Every post on this objection, in the order they were written (a carried copy of an earlier position is flagged `carried`). Each post names its poster (`by`, the seat key) and, where the record can name it, the poster's `maker`.

maker.description: The company behind the poster, for the record only: it is never shown to a judge and never weighed. A model-API seat is named by its model's company; a session seat by the company of the model its answer declared (never by the model the chain asks for). Absent where no company is known (a mock seat, a session answer that declared no model the table knows).

raised_in.description: The label of the call whose reply raised this objection, as in `stages[].label`: the reviewer's blind review, or its re-ask or retry when the objection came from one; for an objection a reviewer named in an exchange post, that post. An objection carried into a later pass keeps the stage it was first raised in. The reply is in `<label>.md` in the run folder. Absent where no stage is known.

raiser_maker.description: The company behind the seat that raised this objection, read from the answer to the stage `raised_in` names, by the same rule as a post's `maker`. Absent where unknown, and on a row that names no stage.

makers.description: Which makers stood on each side of this objection, for the record only, over every round of its exchange in this pass: the distinct known makers of the seat that raised it, of the support posts and of the contest posts it drew, posts made before it was amended included and refused posts left out. A reviewer who supported it in one round and contested it in another is on both sides. A seat whose maker is not known is left out of the list, not guessed.

flags.description: Present only when a raiser reply was not counted: kind raiser_reply_unparsed (the reply could not be read) or raiser_reply_invalid (it parsed but failed the requirement of its kind, named in `requirement`). Such a reply counts as no reply and never closes the objection.

answer_back.description: With answer_back.enabled: for each judge that had objections in the previous round, the round it will see them in, their ids, how many DECLINED reasons the writer gave and how many passages of the draft changed. Summary only. Present only on such chains. Added in 0.8.2 (src/answer-back.js). On a layered chain a judge keeps its open objections until it is next asked, so a row is written in the round the judge is shown them (not the round after the revise) and `raised_round` names the round it first raised them (0.8.3).

signed_text.description: 0.8.2 (A3/F1): the run's last draft when the review rounds end: its sha256 and whether the panel signed it (in a round where no seat could be heard the draft was shown but nobody read it). When it did not, label is 'not_accepted' and open_objections says how many objections were still open. On a layered chain, round is the latest round in which that draft was put to the panel, or null if it never was (a run can end before its last draft is put to the panel). On a chain without layers, round is the last panel round, or null if none ran. Present on a finished run. `passed` is not touched by any of this.

delivered_text.description: 0.8.2 (A3/F1): the text delivered (deliverable.md). sha256 is of the whole file; body_sha256 of the model-written body without the harness's own blocks. same_as_signed is true when no model stage changed the body after the panel's last review (a harness note alone does not count). changed_by names the model stages that did (dispute, challenge, final_edit); harness_notes the blocks the harness wrote (dissent_block, dissent_record_block, cold_read_block). re_reviewed is false: the panel is not re-run on a changed text.

summary_block.description: Additive (0.8.4): present only when the handling session added a summary and index block at the top of deliverable.md after the run ended. It is NOT one of the harness_notes, and sha256 and body_sha256 above stay the file and the body the run wrote. `chars` is the length of the block as written to the top of the file (its closing --- line included), `sha256` its hash, `text_sha256` the hash of the session's own text, at the time it was added; a reader takes the first `chars` characters off only when their hash is that `sha256`.

handoff_milestones.description: 0.8.2 (item 6c): present only when the chain sets handoff_contract.milestones. What the $0 lint found in the milestones the handoff seat wrote: the Status line (null when absent), how many milestones were parsed, and the findings (no_milestones, no_status, bad_status, duplicate_milestone, milestone_no_check, check_without_expected, unknown_criterion, criterion_not_discharged, discharge_not_checked, status_not_ready, names_prompt_only_section). A finding never changes passed.

status_set_by_harness.description: 0.8.4: present only when the harness replaced the Status word the handoff seat wrote (ready_for_build or partial) with needs_decision, because the run did not agree and nobody had accepted the plan as it stands. `status` stays the seat's own word; HANDOFF.md carries needs_decision and a note line under it.

split_contract.description: 0.8.3 (M3): present only when the plan holds a block marked the-high-council:tree-split. What the $0 block-local checks of the split contract found: the sha256 of the block as canonical JSON (null when it does not parse), whether every check passed, and the findings (the check number, a stable rule name and the words). It never changes `passed`; the tree applies the checks that need it (an ancestor's obligations and questions) again at expansion.

plan_checks.description: 0.8.4: present only when the run delivered a plan. What the two information checks of the plan's own body found, one entry per check that was asked for. `claim_markers` flags a statement about the project that carries none of the four markers (CHECKED, UNVERIFIED, DISPUTED, ABSENT), a DISPUTED marker no dispute pass wrote, and a CHECKED marker whose cited range or excerpt no seat was shown; `test_identifiers` lists the names a fenced test file of the task uses that the plan never mentions. A check that ran has `ran: true` and its `findings` (an empty list means it ran and found nothing); a check that did not run has `ran: false` and `reason` `no_plan_body` (the delivered file could not be separated from the notes above the plan by the report's own record); a check that was not asked for has no entry, so an absent entry is not an empty one. A finding never changes `passed`, the exit code or any text, and nothing reads this field to decide anything.

verdict_envelope.description: Present (true) only on a run that used the verdict envelope: each critic call carried a fresh review_id and draft_id, recorded in `<label>.envelope.json`, and a reply without them was not read as a verdict. Absent means the run did not use it.

tree.description: 0.8.3 (M6): present only on a member run of a recursive-councils tree: the member's lineage, copied unchanged from the `tree` field of its run.json. treeId is the run id of the tree's root run (the folder that holds `tree/`); node is the logical position, a path of milestone ids from the root (R, R/M2, ...); generation counts how often a decision has replaced that node (1 = the first); attempt counts starts of the same node and generation; parentNode and depth place it in the tree (null for the root); splitSha256 is the hash of the split block the node was derived from and bundleSha256 the hash of its input bundle (null where the tree has not computed them). A run that is no tree member has no `tree` key.

thin_contract.description: 0.8.2 (item 6a, the thin contract): one record of what this run was asked, graded against, shown and signed, all full-width sha256. task_sha256, criteria_sha256 and checks_sha256 repeat the fields of the same names; signed_text_sha256 is signed_text.sha256 (item 4). evidence.context_sha256 is the hash of the --context documents as the harness appended them (null when there were none); evidence.ground_truth_sha256 is the hash of the tool results the run recorded as shown (null when none), canonical JSON of each { tool, args, result } without result_ref. `sha256` is over the record without that field: canonical JSON, keys sorted at every depth, no whitespace, UTF-8, an unknown component the literal null. Tamper-evident, not tamper-proof: `council contract check <run>` recomputes what the folder still holds. Absent for an advice run and for a run with no criteria, task text or signed text.

handoff_text.description: 0.8.2 (F1): present when the chain has a handoff stage. made_from_sha256 is the text the handoff stage was given; made_from_signed is true only when that is exactly the text the panel signed; panel_reviewed is false (no panel reads a handoff). file_sha256 is the sha256 of HANDOFF.md as written, banner and lock block included; it is present only when this run wrote that file (a --rematch or --replay report has no file_sha256). Since 0.8.4, once `council note-add` has added a note to HANDOFF.md, file_sha256 is the sha256 of HANDOFF.md as it now is (with its notes section) and file_sha256_at_end, present only then, is the sha256 of the file as the run wrote it; `council contract check` compares file_sha256_at_end with the file after taking the notes section out.

open_objections.description: 0.8.4, additive: present only when the chain has a handoff stage and the run ended agreed on the handling session's build check with `passed` false and objections still open. One row for each of those objections, as the handoff prompt listed them for its seat: the objection's id, the layer that raised it, the rating in force and the problem as the judge wrote it (`layer` and `severity` are null where the record has none). `council handoff --from-run` reads these rows back for its own prompt.

ending_exchange.description: 0.8.4: the ending exchange, present only when a layered run ended WITHOUT the top layer's sign-off (a finish, the round cap, or, in a run with no handling session, the rule that ends it at a stop: trigger rule, 0.8.4, a closed enum widened) with a layer-1 objection still marked not_debated. It is not a pass: no blind review, no sign-off, no revision, and it changes no plan text (an amend changes the record's text only). ran false with not_run fewer_than_two_heard: fewer than two layer-1 judges were heard in the last pass that asked layer 1, so nothing ran and the objections stay not_debated, flagged. `objections` are rows like layer_debates[].objections; `still_not_debated` lists the ones that no judge posted on. Labels of its calls: ldebate-end[-xK]-<seat>, lreply-end[-xK]-<seat>.

not_run.description: Why no call was made: fewer than two layer-1 judges were heard in the last pass that asked layer 1; the objections' raisers were not heard; or (0.8.4) the person finished the run at once, so no judge was asked and every objection stays not_debated.

late_findings.description: 0.8.4: defects found where no round follows to debate them: in the LAST (seventh) round of the ending exchange (found is ending_exchange_last_round), or by a top-layer seat, a new defect that no listed item names: at its final read (found is final_read) or in its sorting at its last verdict (found is last_verdict). Not objections: they mint no objection id, hold no sign-off, count in no tally and are never dropped, declined or debated; they are marked not_debated and shown to the handler (BOARD, HANDOFF). id is L- and eight hex digits over the seat, the criterion and the normalised text, with #2, #3 for a collision. rating is the finder's own, 1 to 10 with one decimal; null when it was missing or refused (rating_refused says why), and then it reads as 4 or above for the handler's order (rating_read_as). flags: ungrounded (no criterion, no quote, or a quote the plan does not hold; kept) and named_as_objection (written in new_objections in the last round, where nothing may be minted; kept) and named_in_final_read (found by a top-layer seat at its final read; kept) and named_in_sorting (named by a top-layer seat only in its sorting at its last verdict; kept). sorted is the top layer's sorting of it: null until it is sorted (and while no top-layer seat has sorted it must-do and not every top-layer seat has sorted it may-leave), then { sort, seats, reasons }, with ungrounded when its must-do names no criterion and no decision. The words are the finder's, as they came. The list also holds, marked dropped_after_check, a late finding that a build check demanded and that the last verdict no longer carries.

linked_to.description: 0.8.4, additive: present on a late finding made from an unanchored failure (one that quotes nothing) that a top-layer seat sorted must-do. ONE late finding is made per failure, however many seats sorted it: its id is made from the failure's own seat and text (so it does not change when a seat words its reason again), its reasons are every sorting seat's words and its rating is the highest rating a seat gave it. The failure's own id stays open, flagged unanchored, and keeps the seats' sorting as a record only; the build list's must-do item is the late finding. The build check names the pair once, by either id.

demanded_in.description: 0.8.4, additive: the numbers of the build checks that listed this late finding and demanded it by id (build_checks[].n for a check that was answered); present only when a check did. Rebuilt on every resume from the replayed passes, never recorded separately.

dropped_after_check.description: 0.8.4, additive: a build check demanded this late finding, and the top layer's last verdict no longer carries it (a later verdict dropped it or worded it again, which gives a new id). The row stays so that build_checks[].required resolves; the build list, the board and every count show only the late findings that are still carried.

route.description: Additive (0.8.4): the repair route the seat named for a must-do: writer, or proposers (the decision would go back to the proposers). A closing read only recommends it; nothing is sent back at a read. On a combined row: proposers when any seat's must-do named it, else writer.

route_asked.description: Additive (0.8.4): proposers, when a seat asked for the proposers on a chain that has no proposer seat; the route is then recorded as writer and nothing is asked again.

route_unread.description: Additive (0.8.4): what the seat wrote as the route when it was neither writer nor proposers; it is not read as a route.

writer_notes.description: 0.8.4: the writer's fix note of each revise pass of a chain with answer_back, present only when at least one row exists. The rows are built from the writer's own lines and nothing else: a FIX-TAKEN line (taken judge_line or writer_own, with the passage the writer says it changed) or a DECLINED line (taken declined, with its reason and no passage); an id named by both is conflicting; an objection with no line has no row. The passage and the reason are the writer's claims, not checked. judge_fix is the judge's own fix line, kept beside the writer's note and the raiser's answer (answer_back_replies, severity.withdrawn[].cleared_by).

answer_back_replies.description: With answer_back.enabled: what each judge said about its own earlier objections (the `answers` array of its reply) and what the harness did with it: withdrawn (a quote from the draft was given), withdrawal_refused (no usable quote found: the objection stays open, and refusal says why), sustained, unknown_id, unreadable_answer (a status that is neither sustained nor withdrawn: the objection stays open), unanswered (no answer at all: since the release after 0.8.2 the judge is asked once more when it signed off clean, and an objection still unanswered stays open, in signoff[].objections with carried_from_round). Present only when there were answers or own objections to answer. Added in 0.8.2. stated_pass_open (0.8.3, layered chains): the judge stated a pass while it still held this objection; a pass is not a withdrawal, so the objection stays open and that pass does not count as sign-off. quoted_from, quoted_ref, quoted_layer (0.8.3, layered chains with answer_back): on a withdrawn row, no quoted_from means the quote was found in the current draft; quoted_from "reviewer" means it was found in another judge's recorded row, named by quoted_ref (the lab) and quoted_layer (that row's layer), and the three appear together or not at all.

spans.description: 0.8.4, additive, only on a `sustained` row whose evidence quotes anything: the quoted passages of the judge's evidence, each once and at least 8 characters once normalised, each with `located_in`, the first of `draft`, `fenced_source`, `excerpt`, `request` and `criteria` that holds it, or null. The same marks as an objection's `spans`. Record only: the objection stays open as before.

refusal.description: 0.8.4 (additive), only on a withdrawal_refused row: why the withdrawal was not accepted. not_found: the judge quoted a passage of 8 or more characters and none of those passages is in the draft it was shown (nor in a row of another judge that it was shown); too_short: it quoted, but every quoted passage is under 8 characters once normalised; unreadable: no quoted passage could be read in what it wrote as evidence.

effect.description: swept_carried (0.8.4, additive, only when the judges rate their objections; a closed enum widened: a reader that validates `effect` strictly must accept it): the judge left an earlier objection rated below the line that holds a sign-off without an answer; it blocks nothing, so the judge is not asked again for that answer; `path` says whether a verdict or a stated pass carried it. withdrawn_exchange (0.8.4, additive; a closed enum widened: a reader that validates `effect` strictly must accept it): the judge withdrew the objection in its layer's exchange, giving a reason and no quote; it closes the objection like withdrawn, and the objection ledger says so.

path.description: 0.8.4, additive, only on a swept_carried row: how the objection was carried without an answer (a verdict that left it unanswered, or a stated pass that carried it).

debate_orders.description: With debate_hygiene.shuffle: what each debate reader saw - the item ids (proposals, or alternatives) in the order it was shown them and the lab letter each lab had in its prompt. Present only on such chains. On such a chain the free text of debate.posts[] is re-lettered to real ids and lab names, so one lettering reads the whole record. Added in 0.8.2.

criteria_ids.description: Positional ids for `criteria`, index-aligned: C1, C2, ... (0.8.0).

missing_criteria.description: Sign-offs whose criteria table left criteria out (0.8.0). Recorded only: no verdict, prompt or stop reads it. [] when there were none. A reply with no table at all is not listed.

cut_despite_support.description: Proposals the plan cut although another lab supported them in the debate (0.8.0). Derived from proposals[] and debate.posts[]; present only when the run had both.

disagreement_map.description: One row per review round: each lab's verdict and the counts (0.8.0). Derived from panelVerdicts[]. A verdict marked `(carried)` was reused on an unchanged draft.

check.description: The command, test or measurement that settles it (model-supplied).

on.description: plan or build: what the check runs against.

downgraded.description: Why a criterion marked checkable was counted as judgement (it named no check).

criteria_kinds.description: Present only on chains with criteria_kinds.enabled. Index-aligned with `criteria`: whether a named check settles each criterion (checkable) or a reader's judgement does. kind is null when the seat classified nothing.

criteria_summary.description: Present only on chains with criteria_kinds.enabled: counts over criteria_kinds and criteria_met_without_evidence.

criteria_met_without_evidence.description: Present only on chains with criteria_kinds.enabled: every MET verdict on a checkable criterion that cited no evidence. Counted on the board; it does not overturn the verdict.

partial.description: Present, and true, only in report-partial.json: the run did not finish and this is what it had when it stopped. Never present in report.json. Added in 0.7.7.

stoppedBy.description: report-partial.json only: what stopped the run. `overseer_cap` and `layer_bound` (0.8.3): a layered run used all its allowed overseer rounds and the top layer still objected, or a layer needed more than its allowed revisions, or a seat of a layer stayed silent for too many passes in a row; it is resumable, NOT agreed, and exits 23 (the `stop` object says which). `stall_stop` (0.8.4): objections stood unchanged through the stall window and cannot be passed up (the top layer holds one; no pass is left; the chain keeps no answer-back list or does not ask its judges to rate; or the next pass is a ladder pass, which does not pass a plan up); it is resumable, NOT agreed, exits 23 and waits for the person's choice (the `stop` object says which). `owner_pause` (0.8.4): the person or the handler session asked the running run to pause between two passes (`council pause`); it is resumable by a plain `council --resume`, exits 23, and is not a limit. `budget` is the per-run spend cap (--max-usd; exit 4). `user`, `client_cancel` and `wall_clock` were the stops of an advice call (exit 18, 0.8.1); the advice add-on was removed in 0.8.4, so no run writes them now, and a partial report an earlier version wrote can still carry one. A reader must ignore a value it does not know. Added in 0.7.7; values added in 0.8.1.

stoppedAtStage.description: report-partial.json only: the label of the stage the run stopped before (never called, never paid for) - the stage STOPPED-budget.json's `stoppedAt` names. Added in 0.7.7.

reason.description: Why the reply could not be read (status unreadable).

severityRow.description: One objection in the severity record: its id, the seat that raised it, the tag in force and the tag as first valid (`original`), the band (fix, settle, sweep or unreadable) and the state.

seat.description: Present only for a judge that is a repeated seat (the same model on more than one layer): the seat key, where `lab` is the bare lab.

abstentionReason.description: Closed set (RESERVED_ABSTENTION_REASONS in src/chain.js): why a seat gave no usable reply.

default.description: Model-supplied: the answer the plan assumes if nobody answers.

criterion.description: The criterion text this objection is against (or a harness placeholder when the critic named none).

lab.description: Present in lastCritique.failures on unanimous chains: the lab that raised it.

quote.description: A passage the judge gave, or one attached in the exchange: see quote_attached_in.

excerpt_id.description: 0.8.4, additive: present with quote_status in_excerpt; the id of the recorded excerpt (excerpts.jsonl) that holds the quoted passage.

spans.description: 0.8.4, additive: present when the objection quotes anything. One entry per quoted span of the objection, each once and at least 8 characters once normalised: its `quote`, the quoted passages of its problem and its fix, and those of the evidence of the FAILED row of the same criterion in the judge's table (the first such row). `located_in` names the first of `draft`, `fenced_source`, `excerpt`, `request` and `criteria` that holds the span, or is null when none does (a paraphrase, or a passage from an earlier draft, reads null as well). The comparison ignores case, emphasis and quote marks, so it is looser than the quote check, which is case-sensitive: a span can be located while `quote_status` says `unverified`. Record only: nothing is gated or removed, and the objection id does not read it.

quote_attached_in.description: 0.8.4, additive: present when the quote of this objection was not in the judge's own failure but was attached to it in the exchange; the label of the stage whose reply carried it (a raiser's reply, or its own post). The objection keeps the id it was raised with. It does not change quote_status, which describes the judge's own failure.

unanchored.description: 0.8.4, additive: present and true when this objection record quotes no passage of the plan. It says what the record holds (no quote is recorded); it does not say whether the judge was asked for one. Absent when the record carries a quote.

severity.description: Additive, present only when the judges rate their objections: the raiser's own tag, a number from 1 to 10 in steps of 0.1 (null where an objection has no readable tag). Never a default.

id.description: 0.8.2, additive: a stable id for the problem, the same in every round the same lab raises the same criterion about the same quoted text (src/objection-ids.js). Since 0.8.4 an id may carry a suffix: #2, #3 for a new objection of the same lab whose key repeats, #r2, #r3 for one that reopens an objection of the same lab that was withdrawn, overruled, adopted by an upper layer or put below 4 by a re-tag (`reopens` names the old id; an objection the handler or the top layer lowered below 4 keeps its own id).

relation.description: 0.8.4, additive, model-supplied: the relation the judge declared for this failure: new, continues <id> or reopens <id>.

same_key.description: 0.8.4, additive: true when this objection took a suffix because its key repeats an id of the same lab.

reopens.description: 0.8.4, additive: the id of the same seat's earlier objection that this one reopens. A seat reopens an objection of its own that was withdrawn, overruled, adopted by an upper layer or put below 4 by a re-tag, by raising it again: the new objection gets a linked id (`#r2`, `#r3`), and a withdrawal stays on the record. The exception is an objection that the handler or the top layer lowered below 4: raised again, it keeps its own id and carries no `reopens`.

see_also.description: 0.8.4, additive: the id of another judge's withdrawn objection about the same criterion and quoted passage; a pointer, never a merge.

criteria.description: Model-supplied per-criterion table, when the critic gave one.

dropped.description: True when the last critic failed at the provider and the round was recorded as a failure.

provider.description: Deprecated: use `lab`, which holds the same value. Despite the name, this is the seat's LAB (labOf(seat): `lab` if set, else the provider), not its transport provider. Kept for compatibility; removed only in schemaVersion 2.

lab.description: The seat's lab (labOf(seat): `lab` if set, else the provider), the independence accounting key. Added in 0.7.7; absent on earlier reports, where `provider` holds this value.

cut.description: 0.8.4, additive: true on the row of a seat that had answered, in the layer being asked, when the person's finish ended the run (at a pause for a credential-shaped string, or at the spending limit); on a layered chain the run's stop is of kind secret_pause or budget_stop. The reply is the seat's own and stays on the record; it counts for no sign-off and no read. Its objections count as open, except one the seat withdrew in a completed round of the exchange the finish cut: signed_text.open_objections counts the open ones, and where the report carries a dispute record, dispute.open_objections lists them. Of those, one the seat already held open before the finish keeps the row it had; any other is marked cut_off. The withdrawn one is closed: it is not counted or listed, and its withdrawal is recorded in answer_back_replies (where the chain keeps the answer-back ledger) and, unless the objection was first named in a post of that exchange, in the severity record (where it keeps ratings).

signedOff.description: true: signed off. false: objected (see objections). null: gave no verdict - abstained or stated a pass.

objections.description: The seat's objections, on its own record. When signedOff is false, the list gives the reasons for that result. When signedOff is true, the list is [] or (0.8.4) holds only objections rated below 4. When signedOff is null, objections is null.

from_exchange.description: true: named in an exchange post of this pass.

carried_from_round.description: The pass in which the objection was first named, when it is carried.

holds_layer.description: 0.8.4, additive, present only on a seat that STATED A PASS and holds an objection of its own (signedOff null, objections null), so the row would otherwise say nothing of what holds its layer: the seat's own open objections that count in the sign-off, the ones carried from an earlier pass and any it named in an exchange post. The layer is not signed off while this field is present on any seat's row. An objection that holds nothing (rated below the line) is not listed here.

passed.description: True if the seat stated a pass (declined to give a verdict, with a reason). Not the same as the top-level `passed`.

seat_index.description: The seat's index in the chain's seats.critics (0.7.9). A relay panel lists signoff[] in its review order, so array position is not the seat; replay and rematch diffs key on this. Absent on earlier reports.

layer.description: 0.8.3: the layer the seat sits in (seats.critics[].layer). Present only on a layered chain.

id.description: Harness-made: the lab tag in capitals, a counter if the tag repeats, '-', and the proposal's number (e.g. MOCKA-1). The model's own id, if it gave one, is kept as proposer_id.

lab.description: The proposing seat's lab (independence accounting key).

slice.description: The per-seat instruction slice that produced this proposal, if the chain partitions the work.

serves.description: Model-supplied: which criterion or goal it serves.

how.description: Model-supplied; replaced by the author's amendment when amended.

acceptance_test.description: Model-supplied; replaced by the author's amendment when amended.

amended.description: Present and true when the author amended it after the debate.

withdrawn.description: Present and true when the author withdrew it.

replaced_by.description: When withdrawn in favour of another proposal: that proposal's id (checked to exist).

proposer_id.description: The model's own id field, kept for the record.

proposer_lab.description: The model's own lab field, kept for the record.

by.description: Lab that posted, or 'canary' for an injected canary objection.

on.description: Id of the proposal (or alternative) the post is about; never the poster's own.

merge_with.description: With stance 'merge': the other id to merge with (checked to exist).

quoted.description: Only on an objection or merge post of a chain with debate_hygiene.noQuoteMarks: whether the post quotes (a quoted span of at least 8 characters) text that appears in the proposal it is about. false = 'no quote'. Added in 0.8.2 (src/post-quotes.js); detection only, no verdict reads it.

id.description: The author's own proposal (or alternative) id.

replaced_by.description: With action 'withdraw': the id it defers to (checked to exist).

how.description: Model-supplied; an amend usually brings the new how.

acceptance_test.description: Model-supplied; an amend may bring a new one.

reply.description: Built by spreading the model's own reply object and normalising id/action/replaced_by over it, so it may carry more model-supplied keys.

tie_break.description: Experimental. Always { occurred: false } today: no debate step decides by vote yet.

diagnostics.description: Experimental. Role failure-mode diagnostics computed from this run's own posts (src/role-diagnostics.js): perSeat, pairwiseAgreement, roleVsPlainSubstanceGap, flags.

dropped.description: Experimental (0.7.8). Debate posts and author replies the stage's filters rejected, one row per stage, lab and reason; [] when none were. Absent in runs made before 0.7.8. Reasons: for stage 'debate' unknown_target, own_proposal, bad_stance, unreadable, provider_error; for stage 'replies' unknown_target, not_own_proposal, not_posted_on, bad_action, unreadable, provider_error. An 'unreadable' row counts whole replies that did not parse, not posts; 'provider_error' (0.7.9) counts whole replies the provider ended with stop error, content_filter or refusal on the first try and on its one retry.

by.description: The lab whose post or reply was dropped.

status.description: From the plan's 'Scope ledger' line for this id; 'unaccounted' if the plan never mentions it.

built.description: Always null when written: left for a person to fill in after the build session.

reason_code.description: Why the seat produced nothing, in the same spelling as signoff[] and panelVerdicts[]. Written on alternatives dropouts since 0.7.7.

reasonCode.description: Deprecated alias of reason_code, same value; written on alternatives dropouts only. Removed only in schemaVersion 2.

cacheAsked.description: Prompt caching, additive: present only on a call that carried a prompt-cache marker; its lifetime (5m or 1h). input then counts only the tokens AFTER the cached head (Anthropic's own figure).

cacheRead.description: Tokens read from the cache on a marked call; absent when the response carried no count, in which case the count is unknown, not zero.

cacheWrite.description: Tokens written to the cache on a marked call (both lifetimes); absent when unreported.

cacheWrite1h.description: The 1-hour part of cacheWrite, present only when the response split the write by lifetime.

cacheCounts.description: Present on a call that was billed a cache write the response does not state, or whose charge departs from the write count the response reports. "unknown": the response carried no cache counts although the call is billed a cache write: a marked call (charged as a full write of its lifetime) or a call to an OpenRouter OpenAI model of the GPT-5.6 family or later (or one whose generation THC cannot read), which may be billed a write even when none was asked (charged as a cache write of its whole prompt); in both cases the cap errs high. "write-not-reported": a call to such a model whose response carried a cache read count and no write count; the part of the prompt that was not read from the cache is charged as a write and the read count stays as reported. "write-in-input": a call to such a model whose response reported a write count, a zero included; THC counts a written token as lying inside the prompt (checked against the replies of one paid test only, for one model on one host) and charges every prompt token that was not read from the cache as a write whatever the count, so the count did not set the price, and the cacheWrite beside it stays as reported.

cappedAt.description: Optional. The output cap this reply was asked at: the seat's own cap, or the bigger one an Anthropic seat was retried at after its thinking used the whole cap. Present on every stage that went through a call. Added in 0.8.1.

noAnswer.const: no answer: thinking used the whole cap
noAnswer.description: Optional. Present when the reply was cut off at its cap after spending its tokens on thinking and carried no text: the seat has no answer (an unreadable non-pass, never a pass). Added in 0.8.1.

reservationId.description: Optional. The id (r1, r2, ...) of the spend reservation written before the call that paid for this stage was sent (spend-reservations.jsonl), so a charge can be matched to its reservation even when a label was run twice. Absent when the stage wrote no reservation (a mock stage, or a call projected at $0). A cached replay carries the id of the sitting that paid. Added in 0.8.3.

basis.description: Optional (0.8.4). What this stage's `usd` stands for: `token_priced` (THC's own count of the reply, tokens times the price row; never the provider's bill) or `worst_case` (the reply's usage could not be read, so one attempt's worst case was counted). Absent on a $0 stage and on a record from before 0.8.4. The other bases (provider_usage, typical_error, expected_retry, reserved_unsettled) belong to charges of failed attempts and are summed in `totals.counted`.

label.description: Stable stage label; <label>.md in the run folder holds the reply text.

usd.description: What this call cost, including any attempt thrown away and retried.

priced.description: False when the model has no price in pricing.json: usd is then 0 and means 'unknown', not 'free'.

cached.description: True when replayed from <label>.md on disk at no cost.

asked_for.description: Session-seat stages only (provider external): the model the chain's seat asks for (for example subscription:opus-5.5), or claude-code-session when it asks for none. Added 0.8.3, additive.

answered_by.description: Session-seat stages only, when the answer arrived through submit_stage: who answered, AS DECLARED by the MCP client and by the session. Never verified: a client can say anything. Absent when the answer was written as a file by hand. Added 0.8.3, additive.

model.description: The model the session said wrote the answer, or null when it did not say.

declared_by.description: caller: a model was passed; client: only the client's name; none: neither.

persona.description: Optional, experimental. The persona the seat of this stage row is configured with, or null: a judge's `persona` (a bare name) on its verdict and exchange rows, a debating seat's `role.persona` (a key into the persona set) on its propose-, debate-, reply- and canary-reply- rows; null on every other row. Absent on a row recorded without the stamp: a stage file written before 0.8.4, and the demo run `council init` writes. Added 0.8.4, additive.

persona_name.description: Optional, experimental. The name the call's prompt actually carried, noted when the prompt was built; null when the prompt carried none (a judge's persona while the chain's seat_personas switch is off: configured, never sent; every row that is not a judge's or a debate row). Added 0.8.4, additive.

persona_set_sha256.description: Optional, experimental. On a debate row whose seat carries a persona key: the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the persona set that call's prompt was built from (read when the prompt was built, so a persona file edited later does not change it); null on every other row, a judge row included (a judge's persona is a bare name that is never looked up in the set). Added 0.8.4, additive.

model_source.description: Optional, experimental. Where this row's `model` comes from. provider: the id the seat was seated with, as the record writer stores it (not checked against the provider's reply); declared: a session seat's answerer named a model (stored, never verified); undeclared: it named none. Added 0.8.4, additive.

input.description: Prompt tokens that were not read from a provider's prompt cache. Since 0.8.4 this holds for every provider. A direct Anthropic call also leaves out the tokens it wrote to the cache, and so does a Claude call that THC sent through OpenRouter with a cache marker (the response counts the written tokens inside the prompt: measured with Claude Haiku 5.5); for any other OpenRouter call that reports cache counts the written tokens are not subtracted, because the provider does not say whether they are part of the prompt count, except for a call whose cacheCounts is "write-in-input", whose written tokens are left out of this total too: for a run with such calls this total is the sum of the stages' input less those calls' cacheWrite, each such call taking off at most its own input.

total.description: input + output; the cache counts are not in it.

cacheRead.description: Prompt tokens read from a provider's prompt cache, over every stage. Present only when a call that used a cache carried the count, a zero included. Added in 0.8.4.

cacheWrite.description: Prompt tokens written to a provider's prompt cache, over every stage. Present only when a call that used a cache carried the count, a zero included. Added in 0.8.4.

cacheNotReported.description: Present only when a call that used a prompt cache left out a cache count. A call used a prompt cache when it carried a count above zero, carried a cache marker, or was billed a cache write its response does not state (the stage usage field cacheCounts is "unknown" or "write-not-reported"; "write-in-input" alone does not make a call one that used a cache). Lists "read", "write" or both: the counts that at least one such call did not carry. totals.cacheRead and totals.cacheWrite then add up only the counts the responses carried. A count not named here was carried by every call that used a cache, and a count that no such call carried is absent from the totals. Added in 0.8.4.

usd.description: Priced spend only; includes supersededUsd when present.

unpriced.description: provider/model pairs with no price: their spend is not in usd.

supersededUsd.description: Present when stages were paid for and later superseded (a resume that re-ran them).

unreplayedUsd.description: Present when paid stage files that no stages[] row accounts for were found when this report was written (an earlier sitting paid for a label the finishing sitting never asked again); included in usd. Added in 0.8.4.

providerReported.description: Present when the run folder holds a paid OpenRouter record. What the provider REPORTED, shown beside THC's own count and counted in no total: `cost` is the sum of the figures the provider reported for the `attempts` that carried one (the provider documents it as "cost in credits"; its unit is not verified), `thcUsd` is THC's own usd for exactly those attempts, `attemptsWithout` counts paid normal replies that carried no figure (a file from before 0.8.4 reads so). `unverified` is always true: not compared with the provider's own record yet. Failed attempts, which carry no figure by design, are not in `attemptsWithout`. Added in 0.8.4.

counted.description: Present when the run folder holds a paid record. The count-once figure of the folder (src/counted-spend.js, the one reader `--spend`, the stop screens' floor and run_status use too): `usd` counts every paid record once - the usage files, the superseded and charge files, plus the two records that have no file (a reservation no settlement closed, at its worst case, and a settled call whose usage file was never written and whose `reserved` line is in the folder) - so it can be higher than `totals.usd`, whose meaning is unchanged (the sum of the stages' settled usd, the superseded and unreplayed spend). `estimatedUsd` is the part of `usd` that is an estimate, not a recorded figure: a typical cost for an error reply, an expected cost for a failed attempt that is asked again, a reservation counted at its worst case, an attempt counted at its worst case. `bases` is the non-zero amount per basis (token_priced, provider_usage, typical_error, expected_retry, reserved_unsettled, worst_case). `unlabelledUsd` is what records from before 0.8.4, which name no basis, hold. `unknownFigures` counts figures that did not read. An unsettled reservation beside a usage file that carries its id counts once, at the larger of the reservation's worst case and the file's amount. A settled line with no reserved line is damage to the file: it is counted nowhere, and `council --spend` names it. It is THC's own count, never the provider's bill. Added in 0.8.4.
